confirmed.claim: `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED with hard proof. Live source `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8` and `:22` pass `variant="outline"`. The installed producer API `/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-18` declares `ButtonProps` with NO `variant` member — the axes are `emphasis` ("primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"), `tone`, `size`, `iconOnly`, `loading`. glass-ui 7.0.0 (package.json:83). The producer explicitly repudiates the name at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16`: "The tone axis ... NEVER a `variant` member." The compiled Button (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:8-32`) has NO `inheritAttrs:!1` and styles purely off `data-emphasis`/`data-tone`/`data-size` (lines 47-56), so `variant="outline"` falls through Vue's default attribute inheritance as a junk literal DOM attribute with ZERO styling effect; the buttons silently render at the DEFAULT `emphasis="secondary"`, `tone="neutral"`. `size="sm"` IS valid (ButtonSize = xs|sm|md|lg), so only the variant limb is dead. I additionally proved the failure is TYPE-INVISIBLE: `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` ran to completion with zero diagnostics. SCOPE CORRECTION the axis missed: this is not PaginationBar-local staleness but a repo-wide epidemic — 51 `<Button variant=...>` sites across 20 files (e.g. AdminAuditPanel.vue:30,49; AdminUsersPanel.vue:21,32,58,112,122; ProfileSection.vue:59,111,135; BrowsePane.vue:69,136), while the CORRECT vocabulary is already in use elsewhere (`emphasis="text"` at PalettesPane.vue:113 and AdminUsersPanel.vue:174) — i.e. a partially-completed glass-ui 7 migration, not a one-off.

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation; users can repeatedly activate arrows while results load.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the cure is trivially available and unused. `PaginationBar.vue:10,24` bind `:disabled` ONLY to `!hasPrev`/`!hasNext` — there is no busy/pending input at all; the component's prop surface (`:37-42`) has no `loading`. The producer ships the exact affordance: `Button.vue.d.ts:16` `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles" — implemented at `button-Bu9F4uU6.js:35` (`m = loading || disabled`) with an activation-suppressing handler at `:44`. The in-flight flag is already published by both ports (`demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:39,96` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:52,138` expose `loading`) and is already consumed for skeletons by the panels (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16), but is never threaded to PaginationBar. Double-activation is executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:51-62` ("C2: double-click Next skips a page and leaves two flights in the air" — asserts page lands on 3 and offsets [20,40] are both requested).

confirmed.claim: Events carry no destination/request identity, so parent and child can race; out-of-order responses are possible.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as to the RACE, but the axis misattributes the cause and therefore prescribes the wrong cure. `PaginationBar.vue:44-47` emits bare `prev`/`next`; handlers are `audit.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:88-89) and `flagged.prevPage`/`nextPage` (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:131-132). The real defect is in the composables: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79` carry NO request-sequence token and NO in-flight bail — every `loadX()` unconditionally assigns `entries/items = res.data` and `total = res.total` on resolve, so two overlapping flights resolve last-wins regardless of which page they were for. Also `loading` is a plain boolean, so the `finally` of the FIRST flight (useAdminAudit.ts:68-70) clears `loading` while the second is still airborne, retracting the skeleton early. Executably reproduced in-repo at `docs/.../AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:27-49` ("C1: out-of-order responses — the STALE page wins (no request sequencing)", asserting `page===2` while `items[0].paletteSlug==="page1-row"`). CURE CORRECTION: putting a destination in the emit (the axis's prescription) does not fix this — the child would still be a dumb relay and the stale write would still land. The structurally sound fix is a monotonic request-generation token in the composable, discarding responses whose generation is superseded.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; page values outside [1,pageCount] are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ONLY for the `page > pageCount` limb; the other limbs are unreachable (see killed C-1-limbs). `PaginationBar.vue:3` guards solely on `pageCount > 1` and `:18` interpolates `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}` with no clamp. `page > pageCount` IS reachable in the live tree via the un-clamped local decrement in `useAdminFlagged.ts:87` / `:99` (`total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` with no page clamp and no reload). Worked example: pageSize 20 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:51`), total 41, page 3 → pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(41/20)) = 3 (`:55`); dismiss one row → total 40 → pageCount 2 while page stays 3 → the bar renders (2 > 1) and literally reads "Page 3 of 2". Here `hasNext=false`, `hasPrev=true` (`:56-57`) so the user can still escape via Previous — which is why this variant is MAJOR and not the BLOCKER; the unrecoverable sibling case is filed separately under MISSED.

confirmed.claim: aria-live announces page-text mutations that are not bound to completion of the corresponding list request.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED structurally. `PaginationBar.vue:17` marks the counter `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`, and `:18` renders `page` directly. `useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` (`nextPage`) increments `page.value++` SYNCHRONOUSLY and only then calls the async `loadAuditLog()`; identical shape at `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110`. Vue flushes the reactive text update on the next microtask tick, long before the network promise resolves, so the region announces "Page 3 of 5" while the panel is still showing the previous page's rows (or, once `loading` flips, skeletons at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38). The announcement is therefore bound to intent, not to commit. Severity held to MINOR: announcing navigation intent is a defensible pattern and no false content is spoken — the counter is accurate about the requested page. Whether a real screen reader's queueing makes this audible as a mis-ordering is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE (no AT available under probe parsimony). Motion/PRM law is not implicated: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274` lists PaginationBar C·D·L under "§7.4 No motion content — vacuously cleared", so no M-xx row constrains any verdict here.

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances, and no threshold or large-count design exists.
confirmed.proof: Factually CONFIRMED but NOT a defect at the shipped scale — recorded at INFO to prevent it being carried as remediable. `PaginationBar.vue:7-29` contains exactly three children: prev Button, counter span, next Button. There is no first/last control, no page jump, no ellipsis range. However both consumers page at `pageSize = 20` (`useAdminAudit.ts:38`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:51`) over admin-scale collections (audit ledger, flag queue), and the repo carries an explicit standing edict against speculative structure (MEMORY `feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md`: "Don't create new shared/ dirs or wrapper components that don't exist yet; KISS"). Building a large-count design for a surface with no evidenced large-count usage would violate that edict. The honest finding is the absence of a documented threshold, not the absence of the controls.

killed.claim: `hasNext`/`hasPrev` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled; the four scalars can contradict each other.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the contradiction is unreachable in the live tree, and the axis reached this verdict only because it declared itself "Source-only" (challenge-C-implementation.md:3, challenge-L-library.md:3) and never opened the two files that produce the props. There are exactly two call sites, and BOTH derive all four scalars from the same two numbers. `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44-46`: `pageCount = computed(() => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize)))`, `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)`, `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)`. Byte-identical derivation at `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57`. These are `computed` refs, not free-floating booleans, so "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" would require `1 > 1` to evaluate true. The bindings are direct (AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130) with no transformation. The "four unrelated scalars" framing further presumes a library boundary that does not exist: PaginationBar is a PRIVATE component — `grep -rn PaginationBar demo/ --include=*.ts` returns zero hits, and the admin barrel `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:3-7` exports only the five panels, deliberately ("NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"). No external caller can supply a contradictory Cartesian product. NOTE: the ONE genuinely reachable inconsistency (page > pageCount) does not arise from untrusted props at all but from the composable's un-clamped delete path — filed as confirmed C-1 and as the MISSED blocker.

killed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel [through a stale axis] — framed as part of the defect.
killed.refutation: REFUTED as a defect. The forwarding barrel is the SANCTIONED, uniform house pattern, not staleness. `demo/ui/button/index.ts` is a one-line `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`, and all 20 sibling primitives follow it identically (`demo/ui/{alert,avatar,badge,card,checkbox,collapsible,dialog,dropdown-menu,input,label,popover,radio-group,select,separator,...}/index.ts`). The pattern is explicitly ruled and documented at `demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9`: the barrel "previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation ... B.W2 (A.W7 idiomatic-gestalt finding N1) converted it to a re-export: glass-ui is the design system, the demo consumes its Alert, not a hand-rolled copy." This matches the standing edict in MEMORY (`feedback_glass_ui_first_class.md`). PaginationBar.vue:34 consuming `../../../ui/button` is therefore correct and conformant. Only the `variant` limb of this bullet survives (confirmed as L-1); conflating the two would send a fixer to unwind correct architecture.

killed.claim: `page=0`, negative values, or non-integer values are rendered verbatim.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — these three limbs are unreachable. `page` is initialised to `1` (`useAdminAudit.ts:37`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:50`) and the ONLY mutations are `page.value++` behind `if (hasNext.value)` and `page.value--` behind `if (hasPrev.value)` (`useAdminAudit.ts:73-85`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117`), plus a reset to the literal `1` at AdminAuditPanel.vue:114. Since `hasPrev = page > 1` gates every decrement, `page` can never reach 0 or go negative; since every mutation is ±1 from the integer 1, it can never be non-integer. Likewise `pageCount` can never be zero or negative: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(...))` (`useAdminAudit.ts:44`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:55`) pins it to ≥1 and `Math.ceil` pins it to an integer. Only the `page > pageCount` limb is live (confirmed separately).

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: REFUTED AS STATED (though it gestures near the real defect). (a) The "invalid negative/zero totals" limb is impossible: `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55, useAdminAudit.ts:44) cannot yield ≤0. (b) The loading and error limbs are already discharged by the PANELS, which own dedicated branches: skeletons at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16-18 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38 and a distinct error EmptyState at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 / AdminAuditPanel.vue:42-53, both carrying provenance comments ("W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger"). Hiding a pagination control when there is exactly one page is standard correct behaviour, not a conflation. (c) The "unknown count" limb is vacuous: `total` is initialised to 0 and only ever assigned from a resolved response, so pre-load state is covered by the loading branch. The genuine harm of the `pageCount > 1` guard is NOT ambiguity of meaning — it is that the guard removes the user's only escape control at the exact moment they need it, which this axis did not see; filed as the MISSED blocker.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the premise is counterfactual. There is no other paginated surface to diverge from: PaginationBar.vue is the sole pagination component in the tree (`find demo/ -iname '*pagination*'` returns exactly one file) and it has exactly two consumers, AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133, both of which route through this same component and therefore through this same live region at `PaginationBar.vue:17`. Divergent announcement phase across surfaces is impossible while the component remains the single implementation. The finding describes a risk of a future second implementation, not a live defect. (A real, different a11y defect in this same live region — that it is nested inside the `v-if` and so is absent at mount — is filed under MISSED.)

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel; target a `PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error` ADT.
killed.refutation: REFUTED on both limbs. (a) FACTUAL ERROR in the premise: it is NOT implemented "independently in each admin panel" — there is exactly ONE implementation (PaginationBar.vue), imported by both panels (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144). There is no duplication to extract. (b) The prescribed cure is not structurally supported: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no Pagination primitive — `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/` lists 60 components and contains none (the nearest, `pager-dots`, is carousel dot-indicators, a different control), so this is not the `feedback_glass_ui_first_class` case of hand-rolling a copy of a shipped primitive. Promoting a 48-line private component with two same-directory consumers into a producer package or inventing a new shared collection package directly contradicts the standing owner edict (MEMORY `feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md`: "Don't create new shared/ dirs or wrapper components that don't exist yet; KISS"). The ADT target is likewise premature: the component's actual defects (dead `variant`, missing `icon-only`, missing `loading`, un-clamped page) are all fixable in place by using props the producer already ships. Extraction would be motion without remedy.

missed.claim: BLOCKER — the `pageCount > 1` guard removes the ONLY escape control at the exact moment it is needed: emptying the last page of the flag queue permanently strands the admin on a dead page, showing "No flagged palettes." and a nonzero flag count simultaneously, unrecoverable for the session without a browser reload.
missed.proof: All three axes missed this because all three declared themselves "Source-only" and never opened the composables. Exact mechanism, fully static-provable: (1) `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:86-87` (`dismiss`) and `:98-99` (`deletePalette`) mutate state LOCALLY — `items.value = items.value.filter(...)` and `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` — with NO refetch and NO page clamp. (2) `demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:90` and `:98` wire these straight from the template, and the panel's only load is `onMounted(() => flagged.loadFlagged())` at `:152` — nothing reloads after a moderation action. (3) Worked case: pageSize 20 (`useAdminFlagged.ts:51`), total 21, page 2 (one row on the last page). Dismiss it → items `[]`, total 20 → `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(20/20)) = 1` (`:55`) while `page` stays 2. (4) `PaginationBar.vue:3` `v-if="pageCount > 1"` is now FALSE → the entire bar, including the Previous button (`:7-15`) that `hasPrev = page > 1` (`:57`) still reports as enabled, is UNMOUNTED. (5) `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37-41` renders EmptyState "No flagged palettes." while `:5-7` simultaneously renders "20 flagged" — the panel contradicts itself on screen. (6) The trap is PERMANENT for the session: the Refresh button (`:10`) calls `loadFlagged`, which computes `offset = (page-1)*pageSize = 20` (`:67`) against a 20-item collection and returns empty again, re-confirming pageCount 1; `grep -rn 'page.value = ' demo/palettes/` finds exactly ONE reset in the whole tree — `AdminAuditPanel.vue:114`, which belongs to the AUDIT panel's filter watcher — so `flagged.page` has no reset path at all once the bar is gone. (7) The state is a composition-root singleton (`demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:73` `const flagged = useAdminFlagged()`, provided at `:245`), so it survives panel unmount/remount; only a full page reload clears it. CORROBORATION: an executable repro already exists in a SIBLING component's corpus and explicitly cites this component — `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts:64-84`, test "C3: emptying the last page STRANDS the panel — empty list, total>0, pagination bar gone", whose line 72 reads `const paginationBarRendered = f.pageCount.value > 1; // PaginationBar.vue:3 v-if` and asserts `toBe(false)`. So the megatranche already holds proof of this defect, yet ZERO of PaginationBar's three axes carry it. The audit panel is NOT affected (no delete path; its filter watcher resets page to 1), so the blocker is specific to the flag queue. Minimal sound cure: clamp in the composable — after any local decrement, `if (page.value > pageCount.value) page.value = pageCount.value` followed by `loadFlagged()`; the `v-if` guard may stay.

missed.claim: MAJOR — the two icon-only buttons never set the producer's `iconOnly` geometry axis, so they render with text-button padding and forfeit the shipped square-target/hit-area treatment, despite the repo using the correct prop elsewhere.
missed.proof: The L axis found the dead `variant` but stopped there and missed the affirmative prop that IS required. `PaginationBar.vue:7-15` and `:21-29` render Buttons whose sole child is an icon (`<ChevronLeft class="h-4 w-4">` / `<ChevronRight ...>`), with `aria-label` supplied — i.e. textbook icon-only commands. The producer ships a dedicated axis for exactly this: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:17` — `iconOnly?: boolean` — "Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command." The compiled component consumes it at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:52-53`, emitting `data-icon-only` and, notably, `data-control-target` (the hit-target hook) ONLY when set. PaginationBar sets neither, so both attributes are absent and the buttons fall to default non-square geometry. This is not a speculative API: the repo already uses the kebab template form correctly in comparable icon buttons — `demo/palettes/browser/slug/PaletteSlugBar.vue:20` and `:32`, `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:65`, `demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:166` and `:176` (21 `icon-only` occurrences across demo/). Same root cause as L-1: an incomplete glass-ui 7 migration, invisible to `vue-tsc` (demo typecheck ran clean) because the prop is optional. Cure is one attribute per button, no structural change.

missed.claim: MINOR — the `aria-live` region is nested INSIDE the `v-if`, so it is created together with its first content and destroyed/recreated on every pageCount 1↔2 transition; a live region must pre-exist its mutations to announce reliably.
missed.proof: Missed by C-5 and D-4, which both reasoned only about announcement TIMING relative to the request, never about region LIFETIME. `PaginationBar.vue:2-3` opens the wrapper `<div v-if="pageCount > 1">` and the live region at `:17` (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) sits inside it, closing at `:30`. Consequence: when a collection grows from one page to two, the region is inserted into the accessibility tree already populated with "Page 1 of 2" — assistive tech generally does not announce content present at region-creation time, only subsequent mutations — so the transition into a paginated state is silent. Symmetrically, when pageCount drops to 1 the region is torn out of the DOM, which is also the mechanism of the BLOCKER above. Ordinary page-to-page stepping (region already mounted, text mutates) does announce correctly, which is why this is MINOR rather than MAJOR. Whether a specific screen reader suppresses the mount-time content is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE under probe parsimony; the DOM lifetime itself is statically certain. Cure: hoist the live region outside the `v-if` (or swap `v-if` for `v-show` on the wrapper) so the region is stable for the panel's lifetime.

missed.claim: INFO — the megatranche's own executable repro/probe tests live under `docs/` and fall OUTSIDE the vitest include globs, so none of them are ever executed by the suite; the audit program's evidence cannot regress-guard the defects it proves.
missed.proof: Discovered while attempting to execute the corroborating repro. `vitest.config.ts:21` sets `include: ["test/**/*.ts", "demo/test/**/*.ts"]`. The audit evidence lives elsewhere: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminFlaggedPanel/repro/flagged-composable.test.ts`, `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/AdminAuditPanel/pi/probe.test.ts`, `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/VersionHistoryDrawer/evidence-C2/vhd-probes.test.ts`. Running `npx vitest run docs/.../flagged-composable.test.ts` returns "No test files found, exiting with code 1" with vitest echoing the include globs. These files are well-built (proper mocks, deferred promises, explicit assertions) and encode real proven defects — including the BLOCKER above — yet they are inert: they will neither fail when a defect is reintroduced nor break when the composable API drifts, and they use absolute `/Users/mkbabb/...` mock paths (flagged-composable.test.ts:10-17) that would not survive relocation as-is. Note this is an observation about the audit corpus's durability, not a product defect; recorded because my lens is code/contract health and because a fixer landing the BLOCKER cure would otherwise have no regression gate available.

missed.claim: INFO — all three axes audited a props-only leaf "Source-only" and never read the two files that produce its props, which is the common root cause of every false finding above and of the missed BLOCKER.
missed.proof: Method finding, offered to calibrate future re-reads rather than as a product defect. Each axis states the restriction in its own receipt: `challenge-C-implementation.md:3` ("Source-only."), `challenge-D-design.md:5` ("Source-only."), `challenge-L-library.md:3` ("Static audit only."). PaginationBar.vue is 48 lines with zero internal state — `defineProps` at `:37-42`, `defineEmits` at `:44-47` — so essentially all of its behaviour is determined by `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts`, neither of which any axis cites. The measurable cost: three findings assert contradictions among the four props that the derivations at useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 / useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 make arithmetically impossible (killed C-2/L-2, C-1-limbs), one asserts duplication across panels that does not exist (killed L-5), one asserts sibling paginated surfaces that do not exist (killed L-4) — while the one genuinely severe, session-permanent, user-trapping defect lives 30 lines into a file none of them opened. For a props-only leaf, the caller set is not context, it is the specification.

unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether a real screen reader audibly announces the counter mutation BEFORE the corresponding rows commit (confirmed C-5/D-4). The DOM/reactivity ordering is statically certain (useAdminAudit.ts:73-78 increments synchronously, then awaits), but actual AT queueing/coalescing behaviour requires live assistive technology, which probe parsimony and the no-browser-tooling law forbid here.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether a screen reader suppresses the mount-time content of the `v-if`-nested live region (missed MINOR). The region's DOM lifetime is statically proven from PaginationBar.vue:2-3/17/30; the announcement outcome is an AT-behaviour question.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — D-5's hedged limb that "the visual hierarchy may not match the source." I proved the mechanism statically (variant is inert; buttons fall back to emphasis="secondary"/tone="neutral" per button-Bu9F4uU6.js:11-12,47-56), but whether the resulting rendered weight is actually wrong for this surface is a rendered-pixel judgement requiring a live view.

NOT ASSESSED — cross-browser/forced-colors and touch hit-target sizing for the two chevron buttons. Relevant because the missing `iconOnly` also suppresses `data-control-target` (button-Bu9F4uU6.js:53), but measuring the resulting hit area needs live layout.
superlatives: EXCELLENT — the `demo/ui/*` barrel discipline is a genuinely well-executed architectural decision, and it is self-documenting. `demo/ui/alert/index.ts:1-9` carries the full rationale and provenance in-line ("This barrel previously held a local shadcn-vue re-implementation ... B.W2 (A.W7 idiomatic-gestalt finding N1) converted it to a re-export: glass-ui is the design system"), and all 20 sibling primitives conform to the same one-line re-export shape. A reader can recover both the rule and the ruling that produced it without leaving the file. The L axis mistook this for a defect.

EXCELLENT — the icon-button accessibility idiom in PaginationBar is exactly right and is the paired form most codebases get wrong: `aria-label` on the interactive element (`PaginationBar.vue:11`, `:25`) AND `aria-hidden="true"` on the decorative icon inside it (`:14`, `:28`), so the accessible name is spoken once with no icon-node noise. It carries its provenance comment at `:6` ("W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels"). The same discipline is applied consistently across the admin cluster (AdminAuditPanel.vue:29-31, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:9-11, :97,:100).

EXCELLENT — `tabular-nums` on the page counter (`PaginationBar.vue:17`) is a precise, easily-forgotten typographic choice: it pins digit advance width so the counter does not reflow as page numbers change width (1→10→100), keeping the flanking chevrons visually static. Paired correctly with `aria-atomic="true"` so the counter is announced as one sentence rather than as two mutated numbers.

EXCELLENT (producer-side) — glass-ui 7.0.0's axis vocabulary is unusually disciplined API design, and it explicitly anticipates precisely the mistake this component makes. `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16` documents the tone axis as "the semantic status register (`--<tone>` token cohort); NEVER a `variant` member" — the producer names and forbids the collapsed-variant anti-pattern in the type declaration itself. `Button.vue.d.ts:8-18` follows through with orthogonal `emphasis` (visual priority, "It does not change the command's semantics") vs `tone` (semantic intent), each documented at the property.

EXCELLENT — the `loadError` discipline in both composables is a textbook correct error posture, and rare: `useAdminAudit.ts:63-67` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:71-75` clear the error on success and populate it on failure, and the panels render a genuinely distinct error branch ahead of the empty branch (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 before :37-41). The provenance comments state the invariant crisply — "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger" — which is exactly the failure mode most list UIs ship. Note this makes the flag queue's SILENT dismiss/delete failures (useAdminFlagged.ts:88-90, :100-102, console.warn only) an inconsistency with the surrounding standard rather than an absence of one.

EXCELLENT — PaginationBar is correctly scoped as a small, private, single-purpose leaf: 48 lines, no internal state, modern typed `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` tuple syntax (`:44-47`), typed `defineProps` (`:37-42`), and deliberately withheld from the public barrel (`demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts:1-7`, "NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"). Its defects are all one-line prop omissions; none are structural. This is the right size and the right visibility for what it does.

confirmed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel; `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and stronger than claimed. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:9. Live: `demo/ui/button/index.ts:1` is exactly `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (forwarding barrel confirmed). The installed API is glass-ui 7.0.0 (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json:3`); `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-19` declares `ButtonEmphasis = "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"` and `ButtonProps` = `{emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class}` — there is NO `variant` prop. The compiled component (`dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js`, props block) defaults `emphasis: "secondary"`, and its render emits `data-emphasis`/`data-tone`/`data-size`; `dist/components/button/styles.css` styles ONLY `.button[data-emphasis=...]`. So `variant="outline"` at `demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8` and `:22` matches no prop, falls through `mergeProps` to the DOM as a literal invalid `variant="outline"` attribute, and both chevron buttons silently render at default `emphasis="secondary"`. Additional proof the axis did not have: I ran `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` — it exits clean, so the hard CI typecheck gate never catches this. Not local to PaginationBar: same stale axis at AdminAuditPanel.vue:30,49 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10,29,90, plus `variant="ghost"` at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:95 (also not in `ButtonEmphasis`).

confirmed.claim: Icon-only buttons are named, but intended `variant="outline"` is not the current producer vocabulary; the visual hierarchy may not match the source.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED (same defect as L-1, independently stated). Axis: challenge-D-design.md:15. Live: PaginationBar.vue:8,22 pass `variant="outline"`; `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4` fixes the vocabulary as `emphasis`, not `variant`. D's hedge "may not match" is resolvable statically and resolves against the source: the buttons render at the compiled default `emphasis: "secondary"` (`dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` props block), which per `dist/components/button/styles.css` gets `--glass-bg-rung: var(--glass-bg-quiet)` + a backdrop blur — a filled quiet-glass capsule, not an outline. D's first limb is also verified true: the buttons ARE correctly named (PaginationBar.vue:11,25) with `aria-hidden="true"` chevrons (:14,:28).

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:12. Live: PaginationBar.vue:7-15 and :21-29 bind only `:disabled="!hasPrev"`/`:disabled="!hasNext"` — no busy binding. The handlers gate on position only, never on in-flight state: `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` (`if (hasNext.value) { page.value++; loadAuditLog(); }`) and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110` (identical). `loading` is a live ref in both composables (useAdminAudit.ts:39,51,69) but is never consulted by nextPage/prevPage and never reaches PaginationBar. Concrete: from page 1 of 5, two fast Next activations advance page 1→2→3 and start two overlapping `loadAuditLog()` requests. The cure is already in the producer and unused: `Button.vue.d.ts:15` declares `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles" — and the compiled guard `dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` folds `loading` into the disabled computed and calls `preventDefault()/stopImmediatePropagation()` on activation.

confirmed.claim: Page changes have no busy register. Users can repeatedly activate arrows while results are loading and receive no relation between displayed page text and displayed rows.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, both limbs. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:12. Limb 1 (no busy register) is proven at C-4 above. Limb 2 (no relation between page text and rows) is proven and is worse than D states: PaginationBar.vue:18 renders `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}` from `page`, which is mutated SYNCHRONOUSLY at useAdminAudit.ts:75 before the await at :60, so the sentence flips to the destination page while the rows are still the source page's. Compounding it, in both consumers the row list is NOT part of the loading v-if chain — AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 (`v-if="loading"`), :42 (`v-else-if="loadError"`), :56 (`v-else-if` empty) form the chain, but the entries at :59 are a plain `v-for` with no `v-else`, so during a page change the skeletons and the previous page's rows render simultaneously under a page counter that already reads the new page. Same shape at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16,22,37 vs :44.

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations, which are not explicitly bound to completion of the corresponding list request.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:13. Live: PaginationBar.vue:17-19 marks the counter `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`. Its only reactive input is the `page` prop, and `page` is incremented synchronously at useAdminAudit.ts:75 / useAdminFlagged.ts:107 BEFORE the fetch is issued (`loadAuditLog()` at :76, whose await is at useAdminAudit.ts:60). Nothing sequences the announcement against `res.data` landing at useAdminAudit.ts:61. So a screen-reader user hears "Page 2 of 5" while `entries` still holds page 1 — the announcement is bound to the click, not the commit. Severity is raised by the fact that the rows are stale-and-visible at that moment (see D-2).

confirmed.claim: The live page sentence is useful, yet rapid updates could announce intermediate states before content is ready.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED (same defect as C-5, independently stated). Axis: challenge-D-design.md:14. Live: PaginationBar.vue:17 (`aria-live="polite"`) fed by a `page` ref mutated pre-fetch at useAdminAudit.ts:75 / useAdminFlagged.ts:107. The 'rapid updates' limb is specifically constructible because nothing debounces or gates activation (C-4): three fast Next presses mutate `page` three times, so the polite queue can carry intermediate page numbers that never corresponded to rendered rows. D's closing prescription at challenge-D-design.md:19 ('Announce the page only when the corresponding list has committed') is the structurally correct cure and is not implemented anywhere in the live tree.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard. `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer, or negative values are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED NARROWLY — one limb is live-reachable, the rest are not. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:9. The structural half is true: PaginationBar.vue:3 (`v-if="pageCount > 1"`) is the sole guard and :18 interpolates both scalars verbatim. Of the four enumerated cases, only `page > pageCount` is reachable in the live tree, and it is genuinely reachable via deletion: `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:97-99` deletes a palette, filters `items` locally and does `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` WITHOUT reloading or clamping `page`. With `pageSize = 20` (useAdminFlagged.ts:51), sitting on page 3 with total 41 (pageCount 3) and deleting one row gives total 40 → pageCount 2 while `page` stays 3 → the bar renders 'Page 3 of 2' (guard passes, 2 > 1), with the list simultaneously showing the empty state at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37. REFUTED limbs: `page=0` and negative are unreachable (`page = ref(1)` at useAdminFlagged.ts:50 / useAdminAudit.ts:37, mutated only by guarded ++/-- and `page.value = 1` at AdminAuditPanel.vue:114); negative/zero/non-integer `pageCount` is structurally impossible because `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminAudit.ts:44, useAdminFlagged.ts:55) is an integer ≥ 1.

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances; that may be correct for small sets, but no threshold or large-count design exists.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as stated, including its own hedge. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:13. Live: PaginationBar.vue:7-29 contains exactly three children — prev Button, the counter span, next Button. `defineEmits` at :44-47 exposes only `prev`/`next`, so no jump affordance is even expressible at the boundary. The 'large-count' concern is concrete for the audit log rather than hypothetical: `pageSize = 20` (useAdminAudit.ts:38) over an append-only audit ledger means reaching page 50 costs 49 activations, each a separate network round trip (useAdminAudit.ts:60). Severity held at MINOR because it scales with corpus size, which is not statically knowable, and D honestly flags this ('may be correct for small sets').

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled.
killed.refutation: KILLED. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:10. The premise ('trusted') is true of the component, but the claimed symptom is unreachable: every live consumer derives these from the same refs with the canonical formulas. `demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44-46` and `demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57` are byte-identical — `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)`, `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)`. The consumer set is closed and enumerated: `grep -rn PaginationBar demo/` returns exactly two call sites, AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133, and both pass those computeds unmodified. Because the flags are computed from the same `page`/`pageCount` the component displays, they cannot disagree with the rendered sentence — 'Page 1 of 2' forces hasPrev=false, hasNext=true. This holds even in the stale-page delete case (see C-1), where page/pageCount desynchronise but hasPrev/hasNext stay consistent with both. The contradiction exists only in the prop TYPE surface, never in a live instance.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props.
killed.refutation: KILLED — the stated mechanism is not constructible. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:11. The child holds no snapshot to race with: PaginationBar.vue:12 and :26 emit bare `$emit('prev')`/`$emit('next')` with no payload (`defineEmits` at :44-47 types both as `[]`), and Vue emits are synchronous, so the parent handler runs inside the click before any prop can change. The handler then reads live reactive state, not a passed-in value: `useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` reads `hasNext.value` and `page.value` at invocation. There is therefore no window in which the child acts on a stale `page` — the child never reads `page` for control flow at all, only for display at :18. A real race DOES exist one layer up (unsequenced responses in `loadAuditLog`), but it is invisible to the emit signature and adding a destination page to the payload would not fix it; recorded separately under missed.

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: KILLED — inverted on its two most serious limbs and impossible on a third. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:11. (a) 'invalid negative/zero totals': structurally impossible — `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize))` (useAdminAudit.ts:44, useAdminFlagged.ts:55) floors at 1 and can never be negative or zero. (b) 'loading' and 'error': the bar does NOT disappear in either state — it is a SIBLING of, not a branch in, the state chain. In AdminAuditPanel.vue the chain is :36 (`v-if="loading"`), :42 (`v-else-if="loadError"`), :56 (`v-else-if` empty), and PaginationBar sits outside it at :83 with only its own `pageCount > 1` guard; `pageCount` retains its last value because the catch at useAdminAudit.ts:64-67 never resets `total`. So during loading and after a backend failure the bar persists, fully interactive. Same structure at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16,22,37 vs :126. D asserted the opposite of what the tree does; the real defect is persistence, not disappearance, and is recorded under missed. Only a thin sliver survives — on very first paint total=0 → pageCount=1 → the bar is absent — but that is 'not yet loaded', not the conflation D describes.

killed.claim: `page`, `pageCount`, `hasNext`, and `hasPrev` can contradict each other. A library boundary should accept one normalized pagination state.
killed.refutation: KILLED as a defect (duplicate of C-2). Axis: challenge-L-library.md:10. Refuted by the same enumeration: both and only consumers derive the flags from the displayed scalars (useAdminAudit.ts:44-46; useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57), so no live instance can contradict. The normalization PRESCRIPTION is a defensible design opinion and has a producer precedent L did not cite — `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/data-table/types.d.ts:23` declares `DataTableStatus = "ready"|"loading"|"error"` with a companion `filtered` flag at :39 to keep empty-filtered distinct from empty-set. But that precedent also refutes L's specific target shape at challenge-L-library.md:15 (`unknown | ready({page,count}) | loading({from,to}) | error(...)`), which matches no installed API. Downgraded from defect to API-shape observation.

killed.claim: Events `prev`/`next` carry no target page, query generation, or request identity.
killed.refutation: KILLED as a defect — the observation is true but the prescribed cure is unsound for the problem it names. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:11. The fact is verified: `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` at PaginationBar.vue:44-47. But the harm L attaches to it ('query generation, request identity') lives entirely in the fetch layer, which the emit cannot reach: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` issues `await getAuditLog(...)` with no sequence token and unconditionally assigns `entries.value = res.data` at :61, so a stale response overwrites a fresh one no matter what the emit carried. Putting a destination page in the payload would not add request identity, would not order the responses, and would duplicate state the parent already owns authoritatively (`page` at useAdminAudit.ts:37). The genuine defect here is the unsequenced fetch, recorded under missed.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: KILLED — the divergence it warns of has no live referent. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:12. 'Locally authored' is true (PaginationBar.vue:17). But there is no second paginated surface to diverge from: `grep -rn "hasNext\|hasPrev\|pageCount" demo/` returns only useAdminAudit.ts, useAdminFlagged.ts and the two panels, all routed through this single component. `grep -rn "aria-live" demo/` returns exactly three regions and neither of the others is pagination — ComponentSliders.vue:84 is `aria-live="off"` on a channel meter, ErrorBoundary.vue:20 is `aria-live="assertive"` for errors. Both paginated surfaces therefore announce at IDENTICAL phase by construction. The claim is speculative about a future second implementation, not a defect in the tree.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel.
killed.refutation: KILLED — its factual predicate is false. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:13. The component is NOT reimplemented per panel; it is a single 48-line module imported by both consumers: `import PaginationBar from "./PaginationBar.vue"` at AdminAuditPanel.vue:102 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144. That is already the de-duplicated state L is asking for. The promotion half is also unsupported: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no pagination primitive — `ls node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/` has `pager-dots` (carousel dots) and `data-table`, and `data-table/index.d.ts:1-2` plus `types.d.ts` expose no page/pagination surface — so there is no producer contract to conform to. Promoting a 48-line component with two co-located consumers into the design system also runs against the standing KISS edict (no wrapper components / shared dirs that do not yet exist). Correctly local.

missed.claim: Activating an arrow that then becomes disabled destroys keyboard focus — the standard pagination focus trap. Missed by all three axes.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:10 and :24 bind `:disabled="!hasPrev"`/`:disabled="!hasNext"`. glass-ui renders this as a NATIVE `disabled` attribute for a native button — `dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js` computes `v = { type, disabled: h.value ? m.value : void 0, "aria-disabled": !h.value && m.value ? "true" : void 0 }` where `h = !asChild && as === "button"`, and `as` defaults to `"button"`. So the `aria-disabled` path is unreachable here and the real `disabled` attribute is always used, reinforced by `dist/components/button/styles.css`: `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none; }`. Failure: a keyboard user on page 4 of 5 presses Enter on Next; `page` becomes 5, `hasNext = page < pageCount` (useAdminAudit.ts:45) flips false, the still-focused button gains `disabled`, and the browser blurs it — focus falls to `<body>`, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document. Symmetric on Previous reaching page 1. Note for the cure: because glass-ui hard-codes native `disabled` for `as="button"`, the component cannot opt into the focus-preserving `aria-disabled` idiom without a producer change — this is a glass-ui relay item, not a demo-local fix.

missed.claim: The bar persists and stays fully interactive through the loading and error states of both consumers, so a dead backend renders an error panel with a live page counter. This is the inverse of what challenge-D asserted, and no axis caught it.
missed.proof: PaginationBar sits OUTSIDE the state chain in both panels. AdminAuditPanel.vue: the chain is :36 `v-if="audit.loading.value"`, :42 `v-else-if="audit.loadError.value"`, :56 `v-else-if="...length === 0"`; PaginationBar is an unguarded sibling at :83. Its only gate is its own `v-if="pageCount > 1"` (PaginationBar.vue:3), and `pageCount` survives failure because the catch block at useAdminAudit.ts:64-67 sets only `loadError` and never resets `total`. Failure: the ledger goes down mid-session on page 3 of 7. The panel shows EmptyState 'The ledger is unreachable.' (:42-47) while PaginationBar simultaneously renders 'Page 3 of 7' with both arrows live; pressing Next runs useAdminAudit.ts:73-78, increments `page` to 4, announces 'Page 4 of 7' through the `aria-live` region (PaginationBar.vue:17), and fires another doomed request — advertising navigable pages of a corpus that cannot be fetched. Same structure at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16/22/37 vs :126.

missed.claim: The row lists are outside their own loading/error v-if chain, so stale rows render underneath the skeletons and underneath the error state. This is the mechanism behind challenge-D's 'no relation between page text and rows', which D asserted without locating.
missed.proof: In AdminAuditPanel.vue the `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain terminates at :56 (`<EmptyState v-else-if="audit.entries.value.length === 0" …/>`); the entry list at :59 is `<div v-for="entry in audit.entries.value" …>` with NO `v-else`, making it an independent sibling that renders unconditionally. Failure: pressing Next on the audit panel sets `loading = true` (useAdminAudit.ts:51) while `entries` still holds the previous page, so the DOM shows three `AdminListSkeleton` placeholders (:37) stacked directly above the fully-rendered previous page's rows, beneath a counter that already reads the destination page. On failure the same list renders below 'The ledger is unreachable.' — the panel contradicts itself. Identical at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue: chain ends :37, unguarded `v-for` at :44.

missed.claim: Unsequenced fetches let an out-of-order response overwrite a newer page — the real race that challenge-C-3 groped for and mis-located in the emit signature.
missed.proof: `useAdminAudit.ts:48-71` has no request token, no abort controller and no generation counter; it unconditionally commits with `entries.value = res.data` (:61) and `total.value = res.total` (:62) in whatever order responses arrive, and `loading.value = false` in a `finally` (:69) that the FIRST settling request clears. Reachable because nothing blocks double activation (see C-4): two fast Next presses advance `page` 1→2→3 (:75) and issue two overlapping `getAuditLog` calls with `offset` 20 and 40 (:55). If the offset-20 response lands second, `entries` ends up holding page 2's rows while the counter and `page` ref both read 3, `hasNext` is computed against that wrong page, and `loading` already read false after the first settle. Identical shape in useAdminFlagged.ts:59+. Correct cure is a generation guard in the composable, not a payload on the emit.

missed.claim: The `aria-live` region is nested INSIDE the `v-if` it depends on, so the announcements at the boundaries of the bar's own existence are lost.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:3 gates the whole bar on `v-if="pageCount > 1"`, and the polite region at :17-19 is a descendant of that gated `<div>`. A live region must be present in the accessibility tree BEFORE its contents change for assistive tech to reliably announce a mutation; a region inserted already populated is generally not announced. Failure: on first successful load `pageCount` goes 1→5, so the region and its text 'Page 1 of 5' enter the DOM together and the arrival of pagination is silent. Symmetrically, when a filter narrows results to one page (AdminAuditPanel.vue:111-117 sets `page = 1` and reloads → `pageCount` 1) the entire region is unmounted, so the disappearance of pagination is also silent while the visible layout changes. The fix is to keep the region mounted and empty it, rather than gating it. Exact announcement behaviour varies by AT/browser pairing — see unproven.

missed.claim: No `<nav>` landmark and no accessible name on the pagination container.
missed.proof:
PaginationBar.vue:2-5 is a bare `
` — no `role`, no `aria-label`, no landmark element, and the closing `
` at :30 confirms no wrapper is added elsewhere. The conventional pattern is `
`, which lets screen-reader users enumerate and jump to the control via the landmarks rotor. Failure: on the audit panel a screen-reader user who has tabbed into the entry list has no landmark to jump to the pager and must traverse every row to reach it. Notable because the component is otherwise a11y-conscientious (see superlatives), so this is an isolated gap rather than a pattern — and because challenge-D's own required-cells line (challenge-D-design.md:19) lists 'keyboard/touch' without surfacing it.

missed.claim: The producer's `iconOnly` API — designed for exactly this control — is not used, so the chevron buttons render as wide pills instead of square icon commands.
missed.proof: `Button.vue.d.ts:13` declares `iconOnly?: boolean` — 'Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command' — which is a literal description of PaginationBar.vue:7-15 and :21-29 (an `aria-label`led button whose only child is an `aria-hidden` glyph). Neither call site passes it. Consequence per `dist/components/button/styles.css`: `.button[data-icon-only] { inline-size: var(--button-size); block-size: var(--button-size); padding: 0; }` is not applied, so the buttons instead keep `.button[data-size="sm"] { padding-inline: calc(0.75rem * var(--ui-scale)) }` against `min-block-size: var(--control-h-sm)` — visibly wider than tall, breaking the square icon-command rhythm the design system defines. I explicitly checked and REFUTED an adjacent tap-target concern: `iconOnly` also emits `data-control-target` (`dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js`) which drives `[data-control-target] { min-block-size: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem) }` under `@media (pointer: coarse)` (`dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css:1`), but that guarantee is already met without it, because `dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1` raises `--control-floor` to `var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)` on coarse pointers and `--control-h-sm` is `max(calc(2.25rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))`. So this is geometry/conformance only, NOT a touch-target failure.

missed.claim: Hardcoded Tailwind `h-4 w-4` on the chevrons overrides the producer's scaling glyph token, so the icons stay 16px while the buttons grow by 1.5× on touch devices.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:14 and :28 set `class="h-4 w-4"` on the icons. glass-ui sizes button glyphs with `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph); }` (`dist/components/button/styles.css`); `h-4`/`w-4` does not match `[class*="size-"]`, so both rules target the element, and Tailwind's `utilities` layer is declared after glass-ui's `components` layer (`demo/styles/foundation.css:1` `@import "tailwindcss"` precedes the glass-ui imports at :56-57), so the fixed utility wins on layer order regardless of specificity. Failure: `dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1` sets `--ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5)` under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, so on a touch device the button grows to `max(2.25rem × 1.5, 2.75rem)` = 3.375rem while `--ui-glyph` would have grown to 1.5rem — but the chevron stays pinned at 1rem, leaving an undersized glyph adrift in a 54px control. Using the producer default (or `--ui-glyph`) instead of a fixed utility restores the scaling relationship.

unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — exact assistive-technology behaviour for the live region nested inside `v-if` (missed finding #5). That a live region inserted already-populated is not announced is the well-documented general rule, but the precise outcome varies by AT/browser pairing (VoiceOver/Safari vs NVDA/Firefox vs JAWS/Chrome). The STRUCTURE is proven statically (PaginationBar.vue:3 gates :17); only the per-AT announcement outcome needs a live screen-reader session. Severity could move MINOR→MAJOR if the first-appearance announcement is confirmed lost across all three pairings.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — the rendered visual delta between the intended `variant="outline"` and the actual default `emphasis="secondary"` (L-1/D-5). The API mismatch, the fallthrough, and the resulting default are all proven statically; how far the served quiet-glass capsule diverges from the intended outline (and whether the admin toolbar's visual hierarchy actually misreads as a result) needs rendering. The defect stands regardless — dead intent is confirmed by the type declaration alone.

PRESCRIPTIVE, NOT ADJUDICABLE — challenge-L-library.md:15's target type `PaginationState = unknown | ready({page,count}) | loading({from,to}) | error(...)`. This is a design proposal, not a claim about the tree, so it can be neither confirmed nor killed against live source. Recorded because it is directionally supported by a producer precedent L failed to cite (`data-table/types.d.ts:23` `DataTableStatus = "ready"|"loading"|"error"` plus the `filtered` discriminator at :39) while its specific four-case shape, including the `unknown` case, matches no installed API.

NOT APPLICABLE — motion/PRM. `audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274` lists `PaginationBar | C · D · L` under §7.4 'No motion content — vacuously cleared on this axis', so no M-xx row bears on this component and none was carried. Verified independently against the live source: PaginationBar.vue:1-48 contains no transition, animation, or `prefers-reduced-motion` surface of its own. The producer supplies the only motion (`tap-squish`, `useLiquidPress` press scaling in `dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js`), and it is centrally guarded by `dist/components/button/styles.css` `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .button { transition: none; } }` plus the demo-global neutraliser at `demo/styles/animations.css:184-193`. Correctly clear.
superlatives: EXCELLENT — icon-button naming discipline, executed exactly right. PaginationBar.vue:11 and :25 carry `aria-label="Previous page"`/`"Next page"` while the decorative glyphs at :14 and :28 carry `aria-hidden="true"`. This is the textbook pairing (name on the control, glyph removed from the tree) and it is the single most commonly botched a11y detail in icon-only pagination — most implementations either leave the button unnamed or leave the icon exposed so the name is announced twice. The provenance is recorded in place at :6 (`<!-- W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels -->`), and challenge-D-design.md:15 correctly credits it.

EXCELLENT — `tabular-nums` on the page counter (PaginationBar.vue:17). missed.claim: Inline math is spaced with `mx-1` — an off-ladder Tailwind rung in a stylesheet governed by the phi ladder — and it visibly detaches sentence-terminal punctuation.
missed.proof: LIVE: Markdown.vue:286-289 `p div.inline-block:has(> .katex), li div.inline-block:has(> .katex) { @apply mx-1; }`. Every other spacing in `.markdown-body` reads the phi ladder (`var(--phi-0..4)`), whose own declaration comment at demo/styles/foundation.css:452-457 states the law: "one ladder, never a re-hardcoded arbitrary value." `mx-1` is 0.25rem — on no rung (the ladder is 0.382/0.618/1/1.618/2.618rem, foundation.css:458-462). Worse, it is symmetric and unconditional, so the three sentence-terminal inline formulas — assets/docs/hex.md:62, assets/docs/hwb.md:77, assets/docs/lab.md:74, all of the form `... <Katex ... />.` — get 4px inserted between the formula and its period. This is visible in the design axis's OWN frame: in frames/D-mobile-390.png the line `where e = 216/24389 and k = 24389/27 .` renders with the period floating clear of the fraction. D-13 audited the display block's horizontal axis and D-7 its vertical rhythm; nobody audited the INLINE block's horizontal spacing — the one species that touches prose directly, and the only one where a spacing error becomes a punctuation error.

missed.claim: The component's own AB-1 provenance comment miscites the exact hiding mechanism that K-1 turns on — it names `clip`, the live sheet uses `clip-path`.
missed.proof: LIVE: Katex.vue:37-38 states the MathML layer is "hidden by the same stylesheet — `.katex-mathml { clip; position: absolute }`". The actual rule in katex 0.16.47 is `.katex-mathml{border:0;-webkit-clip-path:inset(50%);clip-path:inset(50%);height:1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}`. The distinction is the whole of K-1 and D-4: `clip`/`clip-path` visually-hidden is the pattern that DELIBERATELY keeps a subtree in the accessibility tree and in the selection, which is precisely why the raw TeX annotation can reach the accessible name and the clipboard. A provenance comment that is the file's own written justification for trusting a vendored stylesheet should name that stylesheet's actual mechanism. challenge-C-implementation.md:48-49 quotes the comment approvingly and checks the annotation but never the hiding property; challenge-D-design.md:640-643 marks the whole MathML paragraph "SOUND — the reasoning in the Katex.vue:34-40 comment is correct." It is correct in conclusion and wrong in mechanism, which is the failure mode a provenance comment exists to prevent.

missed.claim: D-7's gap can never land on a phi rung for a structural reason none of the three named: the scroll port suppresses margin collapse, so the vendored 1em is trapped rather than merged.
missed.proof: LIVE: Markdown.vue:303 applies `@apply overflow-x-auto` to the math wrapper. Any non-`visible` overflow establishes a new block formatting context, so the vendored `.katex-display{margin:1em 0}` (19.36px at the 1.21em inherited from `.katex`, katex.min.css) cannot collapse through the wrapper — it is trapped inside the padding box and ADDS to, rather than merging with, the wrapper's own `padding: var(--phi-1) 0 var(--phi-1) var(--phi-3)` and `margin-block: var(--phi-1)` (Markdown.vue:304-305). challenge-D-design.md:318-322 enumerates the four owners correctly but calls the sum merely "accidental". It is not accidental, it is structurally unavoidable — and that decides the cure: D-7's own prescription at :328-330 ("Zero the vendored `.katex-display` margin at the component root") is the ONLY form that works, because no amount of retuning the wrapper's phi tokens can absorb a margin that is barred from collapsing. Worth stating explicitly so a future seat does not attempt the cheaper fix.

missed.claim: The prescribed FadingScroll cure would leave the sibling overflow species inconsistent, and its fade is unproven against mathematical glyphs specifically.
missed.proof: Two gaps in the cure as written at challenge-D-design.md:410-411. First: Markdown.vue gives code fences the IDENTICAL bare treatment — `pre { @apply bg-well rounded-2xl overflow-x-auto; }` — so converting only the math port to FadingScroll would produce two different overflow grammars in one column, which is the same "parallel species" defect D-5 correctly attacks for error ink (:263-264) and AB-3 already cured for --muted vs --well. The cure must name both ports or it trades one inconsistency for another. Second: a fade mask over mathematical notation attenuates the terminal glyph itself, where a faded `-` and `=` are confusable in a way a faded code identifier is not — a fade is a safe affordance for redundant text and a lossy one for notation. glass-ui's chunk (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/fading-scroll-DhxXIhm2.js) carries 22 `fade` and 19 `scroll` tokens but 0 `mask` and 0 `gradient`, so the fade is implemented outside that chunk and its interaction with math is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE. This should be decided before adoption, not discovered after.

confirmed.claim: `contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow. Its visual consequences are not part of the design contract.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and PROVEN CONCRETE — the axes gestured, I measured the mechanism. `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52` sets `.palette-card-grid { contain: content }`. Per CSS Containment, `content` == `layout paint style`; `paint` clips the whole subtree at the element's PADDING edge. The grid has NO padding (`class="palette-card-grid grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]"`, :4) so its padding edge == its content edge. Grid items in `grid-cols-1` stretch to full column width, so each PaletteCard's border-box left/right edges COINCIDE with the clip boundary. PaletteCard carries `cartoon-surface` (`demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:19`), defined in `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1` as `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }`, and `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-lead), -5px 5px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-mid), -7px 7px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-contact)` (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1`) — a LEFT+DOWN cast extending up to 7px left and 7px down, at 32-46% ink (`--cartoon-ink-lead: color-mix(in oklab, var(--cartoon-ink) 32-46%, transparent)`). The same geometry is carried a second time by the `.cartoon-cast` child span (`PaletteCard.vue:30`; rule at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css:1` — `position:absolute; inset:0; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)`). CONSEQUENCE: every card's ENTIRE left cast is clipped away, and the LAST card's downward cast is clipped at the grid's bottom edge (the 12px `gap-3` absorbs only the interior ones). The T.W5-R4 cartoon register that `PaletteCard.vue:7-18` is written to celebrate is being amputated by the D.W4 Lane A containment at `PaletteCardGrid.vue:48-52` — a cross-wave contradiction neither wave's own doc records. The pane has 16-24px of gutter (`PalettesPane.vue:27` `px-4 sm:px-6`) so the cast WOULD be visible but for the containment; the grid is the sole clipper.

confirmed.claim: The root has `role=list`, but the comment assumes children use `role=article`; that is not equivalent to `listitem` and is not enforced.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the live comment is wrong twice over. `PaletteCardGrid.vue:3` sets `role="list"`; `:7-8` reads "each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark". Live children: `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22` `role="article"` — confirmed. WAI-ARIA 1.2 gives role `list` REQUIRED OWNED ELEMENTS: `listitem`. An `article` child is not a listitem, so AT computes a list with zero items (no set-size/position). Second error in the same comment: `list` is not a landmark role at all (landmarks are banner/complementary/contentinfo/form/main/navigation/region/search), and neither is `article`. EXTENSION the axes missed: when `empty` is true the grid ALSO owns `EmptyState`'s `role="status"` div as a direct child (`PaletteCardGrid.vue:21-27` → `demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28`), a second non-listitem owned element inside the same `role="list"`. No `listitem` wrapper exists anywhere in the render path. Whether NVDA/VO actually drop the list semantics is the only live-decidable residue; the ARIA contract violation is static and certain.

confirmed.claim: Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied and first-run empty need distinct copy; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED but NARROWED — two of the five states the axis lists are already owned, one is a genuine live bug, and the axis's prescribed cure is rejected. REFUTED HALF: loading and transport failure are NOT missing. `demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:44-54` renders `PaletteCardSkeleton v-for=SKELETON_COUNT` for `pm.browsing`, and `:61-78` renders `EmptyState variant="error"` with a real Retry button for `pm.browseError` — both as v-if/v-else-if SIBLINGS of the grid inside one `<Transition mode="out-in">` (`:40`). So the pane owns the state machine and the grid is a layout leaf; a grid-owned `CollectionSurfaceState` union would duplicate it and violates the repo's standing KISS/no-contrivance edict. CONFIRMED HALF (the real defect, which no axis stated concretely): FILTERED-ZERO wears FIRST-RUN copy at BOTH call sites. `PalettesPane.vue:77-80` binds `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` — `filteredSaved` is search-filtered (`demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:112-114` → `demo/palettes/useFilteredList.ts:8-12`, `items.value.filter(predicate)`) — yet the copy is fixed at `empty-text="No saved palettes yet."` / `empty-hint="Add colors above, then save the set."`. A user with 10 saved palettes who types a non-matching query is told they have none and instructed to save some. Identical at `BrowsePane.vue:83-86`: `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` (search + tier + tags + OKLab color-distance filtered, `BrowsePane.vue:339-349`) against `"No published palettes here yet."` / `"Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall."` The cure is at the call sites (branch the copy on query/filter state), not a typed union inside a 53-line leaf.

confirmed.claim: The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment-root regression.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — and there is a comment in the test suite that falsely claims otherwise. The dependency is real: `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-181` does `sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid>>` then `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined`, fed to `useSortable` at `:183`. The only "guard" is `e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72`, whose comment reads "PaletteCardGrid is role=\"list\" — the B.W1 single-root invariant" but whose assertion is `await expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`. That assertion is INSENSITIVE to root shape: adding a sibling comment/node above the `<div role="list">` in the template makes the component multi-root and sends `$el` to the comment node, yet the div still renders and `getByRole("list")` still passes. So C-5 survives, plus a bonus finding: the test comment overstates its own coverage. No e2e anywhere exercises drag-reorder — `grep -rn "reorder|sortable|drag-handle|dragTo" e2e/` returns zero hits.

confirmed.claim: Default and named slots are unconstrained; the root's list semantics depend on undocumented child behavior.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED only in its ARIA half, which is D-4. `PaletteCardGrid.vue:12` is a bare `<slot />` with no wrapper and no `listitem` enforcement; the required child contract lives solely in the prose comment at `:7-11`. The "undocumented" charge is however partly false — the comment IS the documentation and it is unusually explicit; what it documents is wrong (see D-4). The "unconstrained named slot" charge is separately dead (see the emptyAction kill).

killed.claim: "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter."
killed.refutation: FLATLY FALSE — this is the corpus's worst call, and it is exactly backwards. The relation is live, load-bearing, and three lines long: `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:133` `import { useSortable } from "@vueuse/integrations/useSortable"`; `:180` `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)`; `:181` `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)`; `:183-197` `useSortable(sortableEl, pm.filteredSaved.value, { handle: ".drag-handle", ... onEnd(evt) {...} })`. The grid is bound as that ref at `PalettesPane.vue:76` (`ref="sortableGridRef"`), and the `.drag-handle` the options name is rendered by the grid's slot children at `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:49`. The "folklore" the axis dismisses is also correct Vue: a multi-root component resolves `$el` to its first node, so a leading sibling comment WOULD break `new Sortable(target)`. Worse for the axis — the seam it declared nonexistent is where the component cluster's only BLOCKER lives (see missed #1). REPORT-AUTHORED, evidence count 0 (`registry/HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:269`); the live tree wins.

killed.claim: `empty` can contradict the default slot — a caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither.
killed.refutation: Not reachable in the live tree. Both — and only — call sites derive `empty` from the SAME array they v-for over, so the two are exclusive by construction. `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:77` `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` against `:83` `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`. `demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:83` `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` against `:93` `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`. `grep -rn PaletteCardGrid demo/ src/` returns exactly these two consumers plus the two barrels. The claimed contradictory state has no live producer, and the prescribed cure (a state union inside a 53-line layout leaf) buys nothing the call sites do not already guarantee. This also matters positively: because the exclusivity holds, the EmptyState div never joins the card list as a phantom SortableJS item index.

killed.claim: Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so "a true-empty surface can render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy."
killed.refutation: Two of the three fields are already guarded — the axes did not open `EmptyState.vue`. `eyebrow` has a `withDefaults` default of `"· empty plate ·"` (`demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:90`), and Vue applies `withDefaults` when a prop is `undefined`, so passing nothing yields the default, not a blank. `hint` is `v-if`-guarded (`EmptyState.vue:61`), so it renders NO node when absent. Only `message` is unguarded (`EmptyState.vue:58-60`) — and it is unreachable: both call sites pass all three (`PalettesPane.vue:78-80`, `BrowsePane.vue:84-86`), and `e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-201` and `:203+` assert the exact strings "· empty plate ·" / "No saved palettes yet." and the Browse pair on screen. The residue is a latent API-hygiene wart on `message` only, not the "lost invitation hierarchy" the axis describes.

killed.claim: Arbitrary `gridClass` overrides columns/display/containment/visibility, exports raw styling authority, makes layout testing unbounded, and leaves `grid-cols-1` as the only built-in layout.
killed.refutation: No live consumer does any of this, and the mechanism is misdescribed. Only ONE of the two consumers passes `gridClass` at all, and it passes no layout utility: `demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:87-90` sends `'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')` — a sort-loading dim, nothing more. (`duration-fast` is valid, not a dead class: `--transition-duration-fast: var(--duration-fast)` is bridged at `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/bridges.css:1`, and Tailwind v4's `duration` functional utility resolves via the `--transition-duration` theme key — verified in `node_modules/tailwindcss/dist/lib.js`.) Mechanically, `class="...grid-cols-1..."` and `:class="gridClass"` MERGE into one attribute; they do not "override" — equal specificity means generated-stylesheet source order decides, so the claimed authority is not even reliably available. `PalettesPane.vue:75-81` passes no `gridClass` at all. The grid does guarantee exactly one column today, at both call sites, which is what the narrow pane column wants.

killed.claim: `v-if="$slots.emptyAction"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node; it couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model.
killed.refutation: The premise about Vue is true and the conclusion is empty: the slot has ZERO consumers. `grep -rn emptyAction demo/` returns only `PaletteCardGrid.vue:28` and `:29` — the declaration site itself. Neither `PalettesPane.vue:75-98` nor `BrowsePane.vue:80-118` passes `#emptyAction`. There is no caller to mis-guard, no accessible name to get wrong, and no result semantics to type. The correct finding here is not a defect in the guard but that the guard and the slot are both dead code (recorded as a missed finding).

killed.claim: `EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path; the grid has no shared collection-state primitive for loading/error/filtered empty.
killed.refutation: Both halves fail. (a) The "deep relative path" `../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue` (`PaletteCardGrid.vue:36`) is the ONLY route that exists — `demo/shared/ui/` contains exactly `EmptyState.vue` and `PaneHeader.vue` and has no `index.ts` barrel (`ls demo/shared/ui/`), so there is no seam being bypassed. `BrowsePane.vue:189` reaches it identically. (b) The "no shared collection-state primitive" charge is refuted by the fact that `EmptyState` IS that shared primitive and already carries two typed species — `variant: "empty" | "error"` with `role="status"` vs `role="alert"` and distinct copy registers (`demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:14-27` error, `:28-65` empty, props at `:72-91`) — and BrowsePane consumes BOTH plus a skeleton species (`BrowsePane.vue:44-54`, `:61-78`). Loading/error/empty are separated in the live tree; the axis simply did not look outside the leaf.

killed.claim: "The grid should own a typed state and responsive column policy, while slots provide only card and action content." (required matrix: reorder/drag, selection, partial loading, permission-denied, touch/keyboard)
killed.refutation: Prescriptively unsound for this tree, and partly fictional. `reorder/drag` is owned by the consumer via the `$el` seam (`PalettesPane.vue:180-197`) and moving it inside the grid would REQUIRE the typed adapter L-13 asked for while breaking the single-root contract the grid is built around. `selection` and `permission-denied` have no producer anywhere in the palette feature — `grep` finds no selection state and no permission-denied branch in either pane. `partial loading` IS live and IS owned correctly outside the grid (`BrowsePane.vue:125-131`, the load-more skeleton pair, deliberately rendered as a SIBLING below the grid so the wall does not remount). A 53-line leaf absorbing a ten-cell state matrix contradicts the repo's standing no-god-modules and KISS/no-contrivance edicts.

missed.claim: BLOCKER — drag-to-reorder is functionally corrupt at the exact `$el`/useSortable seam the grid's comment block exists to protect. The move is DOUBLE-APPLIED against a detached array snapshot, so dragging any palette sends it to the BOTTOM of the list and mis-moves a neighbour.
missed.proof: `demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:183` passes `pm.filteredSaved.value` — the UNWRAPPED array, evaluated once at setup — where `useSortable` expects `MaybeRefOrGetter<T[]>`. Chain of receipts: (1) `node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js:13-15` installs `defaultOptions = { onUpdate: (e) => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e) }`; the call site supplies `onEnd`, NOT `onUpdate`, so `...resetOptions` does not displace it and BOTH handlers run. (2) `useSortable.js:78-88`: `const _valueIsRef = isRef(list)` — false for a plain array — so `array = toValue(list)` is the SAME object, and it does `array.splice(from, 1)` SYNCHRONOUSLY, deferring `array.splice(to, 0, element)` to `nextTick`. (3) `node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js:2002-2007` dispatches `update`, then `:2023-2028` dispatches `end` — update BEFORE end, same synchronous `_onDrop`. (4) The captured array is a computed's CACHED PLAIN array: `demo/palettes/useFilteredList.ts:10` returns `items.value` verbatim when the query is empty, and `demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:51-55` defines `savedPalettes = computed(() => getStore().value.palettes.filter(...))` — `.filter()` on a reactive array yields a NON-reactive plain array.
