Recording what is NOT broken, with the comparison that makes it meaningful, is what an L-18 pass is for.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:14 — "The root has role=list, but comments assume children use role=article; that is not equivalent to listitem and not enforced."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and UNDERSTATED — this is not an unenforced contract, it is a live ARIA violation. demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 `role="article"`. `grep -rn 'role="list"|role="listitem"' demo/` returns exactly two hits, both in PaletteCardGrid.vue (:3 and the :7 comment) — there is no `role="listitem"` anywhere in demo/. ARIA 1.2 `list` Required Owned Elements = `listitem`; axe `aria-required-children` (serious). Corroborated live by other seats: registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:24288 (CDP Accessibility.getFullAXTree, 3 seeded palettes → lists `childRoles:["article","article","article"], listitemChildren:0, setsize:null`; `AX listitem nodes anywhere: 0`) and :27348 (both viewports, both engines, 10 cards). The user-visible consequence the axis never states: the saved-palette library announces to AT as an empty list with no set size and no position-in-set. D's own framing ("not enforced") reads as a typing gap and would let a reader close it with a doc comment.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:15 — "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ON THE FILTERED-ZERO LIMB ONLY, and only because it manifests as wrong copy at both call sites. `empty` is keyed to the FILTERED collection while the copy speaks about the UNFILTERED one: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` against :79-80 `empty-text="No saved palettes yet." empty-hint="Add colors above, then save the set."`; `filteredSaved` is search-filtered at demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:112 `useFilteredList(savedPalettes, searchQuery, …)`. With N palettes saved and a non-matching query the pane simultaneously renders the header badge N (PalettesPane.vue:19-25), keeps the delete-all-N trigger (:62-72), and tells the user they have none. Same mechanism at demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:83 vs :85-86. Corroborated live: registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:4847 (5 seeded, query 'qqqzzz', both schemes, 1440 and 390 → header '5', sr-only '(5 saved)', body role=status 'No saved palettes yet.', cards 0, delete-all present) and :5117 (12 palettes). NOTE — the axis's PRESCRIBED CURE IS REFUTED: it asks the grid to own a typed `CollectionSurfaceState`, but the correct architecture already ships one level up (BrowsePane.vue:40-119 renders skeletons / error plate / wall as three sibling branches of one `out-in` Transition, with the error plate OUTSIDE the list and carrying a real Retry at :68-77). The fix is one honest branch of copy at the two hosts, not a state machine in a presentational leaf.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:13 — "The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression."
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, with a sharper mechanism than the axis found. The dependency is real and load-bearing: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-181 `const sortableGridRef = ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid>|null>(null)` → `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement`, fed to `useSortable` at :183. The only stated protection is the comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11. The axis's premise is slightly wrong — a guard EXISTS BY NAME — and that makes it worse: e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71 annotates its next line "PaletteCardGrid is role=\"list\" — the B.W1 single-root invariant", but :72 asserts only `expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`. Adding a sibling comment ABOVE the div would make the component a fragment root and break `$el` while leaving that assertion GREEN — the div still renders and is still visible. Nothing anywhere asserts root arity or that `$el` resolves to an Element. A mislabeled gate is worse than an absent one because it retires the question. Corroborating context: registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:24311 lists "changing `role=\"list\"` to `role=\"grid\"` on PaletteCardGrid" among mutations that keep every configured gate green.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:9 and challenge-D-design.md:11 — "`empty` can contradict the default slot; there is no item count or state union to enforce exclusivity" / "A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither."
killed.refutation: No such caller exists and the prescribed cure is unsound. Both live consumers derive `empty` from the exact collection they iterate, in adjacent lines: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` with :83 `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`; demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` with :93 `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`. There are exactly two consumers (`grep -rn PaletteCardGrid demo/ src/`). Contradiction is not reachable. The cure — "an item count" — is worse than the disease: `$slots.default?.()` returns opaque VNode output (Fragments from `v-for`, comment nodes in dev builds, Transition wrappers), so a node count is not a reliable item count; a leaf that guesses its collection size from slot VNodes is a defect, not a closure. Residue is an INFO-tier API-hygiene note, not the SOURCE-RED verdict at :5/:7.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:10 — "`v-if=\"$slots.emptyAction\"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node."
killed.refutation: True about Vue, inert in this composition. The downstream never branches on slot presence: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:64 renders `<slot name="action" />` unconditionally with no `v-if` and no fallback content (same at :26 on the error arm). Supplying the `#action` template with an empty slot inside and omitting it entirely produce identical DOM. The guard at PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 is dead defensive code with no failure mode. The real defect on this line is the opposite of the one claimed and neither C nor L saw it — the slot has ZERO consumers repo-wide (see missed finding).

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 — "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty."
killed.refutation:
False for two of the three fields. Passing `undefined` through resolves to the child's default under Vue prop resolution, and demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:90 defaults `eyebrow: "· empty plate ·"` and `dots: true`, so the eyebrow and the ghost trio can never be absent; `hint` is `v-if`-guarded at :61. Only the display line at :59 can render blank (one empty `

`), and both live consumers supply it (PalettesPane.vue:79, BrowsePane.vue:85). "Semantically empty" overstates a single empty paragraph with no instance in the tree.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:12 — "The empty copy is entirely optional. A true-empty surface can therefore render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy."
killed.refutation: Same refutation as C-3 and stated more strongly, so it fails harder: "blank annotation fields" is plural and both annotation fields are protected. Eyebrow has a hard default (EmptyState.vue:90), hint is `v-if`-guarded (:61), the trio defaults on (:90). The "careful invitation hierarchy" cannot degrade the way the finding describes; at worst the display line goes blank while eyebrow, trio and hint all still render — which is not a loss of hierarchy but a hole in its middle, and has no live instance.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:12, challenge-D-design.md:13, challenge-L-library.md:10 — "Arbitrary `gridClass` can override columns, display, containment, or visibility" / "The component cannot guarantee card width, reading order, or breakpoint behavior" / "exports raw styling authority … allowing incompatible column grammars."
killed.refutation: Three of the four named override targets are false, and the guarantees said to be missing are structurally present. (a) CONTAINMENT cannot be overridden: `contain: content` comes from the SCOPED rule at PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52, which Vue compiles to `.palette-card-grid[data-v-hash]` — specificity (0,2,0) and unlayered — while any Tailwind `contain-*` in `gridClass` is (0,1,0) inside `@layer utilities`, and layered rules lose to unlayered ones regardless of specificity. (b) CARD WIDTH is guaranteed: `grid-cols-1` with default `justify-items: stretch` makes every card exactly the column width — measured `gridTemplateColumns` 462px at 1440 and 324px at 390 (registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:27312). (c) READING ORDER is guaranteed: single column, source order, no `order-*` and no `grid-flow-dense` anywhere in the file. (d) No consumer sends a column grammar: PalettesPane.vue:75-81 passes no `gridClass` at all, and BrowsePane.vue:87-90 passes only `'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (sortLoading ? 'opacity-50' : '')` — an opacity affordance, not a layout program (`duration-fast` does resolve: `--transition-duration-fast` is bridged at glass-ui dist/styles/theme/bridges.css). The residual — that `hidden` would win the display cascade — is an unexercised escape hatch, INFO at most. The breakpoint complaint also mistakes the composition: both hosts mount this grid inside a fixed ~512px pane column (PalettesPane.vue:2, BrowsePane.vue:2), where multi-column would be wrong.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:14 and challenge-D-design.md:16 — "`contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow or layout participation" / "consequences for overflow, sticky descendants, and positioned affordances."
killed.refutation: Two of D-6's three named casualties do not exist in the live tree, and the one real casualty is never named by either axis. STICKY: `grep -rn sticky demo/palettes/browser/` returns zero hits — there are no sticky descendants. POSITIONED AFFORDANCES: every floating affordance escapes the containment — demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37 `<Teleport to="body">` for the hover panel, and its touch path plus PaletteCardMenu.vue:7 use glass-ui `PopoverContent`/`DropdownMenuContent`, which wrap in reka-ui `PopoverPortal` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/popover-BQGYXZyO.js). Since `contain: layout` only re-parents `position: fixed` descendants and none remain inside the grid, no affordance is broken. What IS broken is the card's cartoon caster — see the missed finding — which both axes walked past while listing casualties that aren't there. A finding that hedges with three plausible nouns and hits zero of the live ones is not coverage.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:9 — "`EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path; the grid has no shared collection-state primitive for loading/error/filtered empty."
killed.refutation: The path limb is contrary to a ratified project decision, not a defect. vite.config.ts:68-71 records it verbatim: "W43 (RF-15) killed the demo `@…` path aliases: every demo import is now relative to its physical home (color-session/palettes/platform/shell/shared/scenes + the feature trees)." `import EmptyState from "../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue"` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:36) is the house form; the only surviving alias is `@src` for reference pages. Faulting a leaf for obeying the alias policy is an audit reading a convention as a smell. The second limb duplicates D-5 and is answered there — the collection-state composition ships at the pane (BrowsePane.vue:40-119), which is where it belongs.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:11 — "Default and named slots are unconstrained. The root's list semantics depend on undocumented child behavior."
killed.refutation: "Undocumented" is false. The child contract is documented in-file at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 — "each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark" — and it is also partly EXECUTABLE: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187 and :203 pin the ratified TRUE-EMPTY child behaviour (trio + dashes, zero fillers) as assertions on both hosts. The defect here is not that the child contract is undocumented; it is that the documented contract is invalid ARIA (D-4). Mis-diagnosing an a11y violation as a documentation gap points the cure at the wrong file.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:12 — "`$slots.emptyAction` couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model; accessible name and result semantics remain caller-owned."
killed.refutation: Dead on arrival: the slot has no callers, so there are no caller-owned semantics to reason about. `grep -rn "emptyAction|empty-action" demo/ src/` returns only the declaration itself at PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-29. The coupling critique is also inert for the reason given under C-2 — EmptyState.vue:64 renders `<slot name="action" />` unconditionally, so slot presence changes nothing. Two of three axes analysed the typing of an API surface that has never been instantiated, and neither checked for a consumer.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:13 — "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter."
killed.refutation: The first limb is factually false and it is the limb the finding rests on. The relation is live, direct and consequential: demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:133 imports `useSortable`, :180 holds the grid ref, :181 reads `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`, :183-197 mounts sortable on that element with `handle: ".drag-handle"` and an `onEnd` that calls `pm.reorderPalettes(ids)`. The consequences are measured elsewhere in the program (registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:1752, :2058 — first-drag ordering wrong, filtered drags corrupting unfiltered order), which is only possible because the relation exists. The surviving limb ("folklore rather than a typed adapter") is real but is C-5's finding, stated better there; carrying it under a false premise makes it unciteable.

missed.claim: The grid's own containment amputates the card's signature cartoon caster. `contain: content` clips descendant paint to the padding box; the grid has zero padding and `grid-cols-1` makes every card exactly grid-width, so the caster's entire horizontal leg is deleted on every card and the last card loses both legs.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 `.palette-card-grid { contain: content; }` — `content` = `layout paint style`, and paint containment clips to the padding box (the element has no padding: :4 `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]`, no `p-*`). The clipped decoration: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:19 applies `cartoon-surface`, defined at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css as `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }`, and `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css) — offset LEFT and DOWN. The demo does NOT override it: foundation.css:366-367 re-points only `--shadow-cartoon` / `--shadow-cartoon-hover` (to `8px 8px`), leaving `-md` at the glass-ui value. The 12-px `gap-3` absorbs the 7px bottom leg between rows but nothing absorbs the left leg or the last row's bottom leg. The two decisions are provably aware of each other and still collide: PaletteCard.vue:9-19 spends ten lines explaining that it declines `overflow-hidden` precisely to protect this caster, and the grid then clips it one level up. Independently measured live by another seat — registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:24803-24815 (D5-03): `gridContain:"content"`, grid `{x:224,w:462}` == card0 `{x:224,w:462}` → `slackLeft=0.00`, `slackRight=0.00`; last card bottom == grid padding-box bottom → slack 0.00 against a 7px extent; two-sample pixel read at dx −1…−12 gives Δluminance 0.0 (identical to bare pane ground) while the bottom gutter resolves 96.8 luminance over its exact 3/5/7px steps. Net user-visible result: the same list renders two different shadow treatments — cards 1..n−1 keep a bottom rule, card n has none. All three axes touched `contain: content` (C:14, D:16) and none named a casualty; D named three, two of which do not exist.

missed.claim: The empty plate is itself an illegal owned child of the grid's own `role="list"`. In the empty state the list owns exactly one child and its role is `status` — a live region, not a `listitem`.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets `role="list"` on the root and :21-31 mounts `<EmptyState>` as a DIRECT child of that root; demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28 hard-codes `role="status"` on the empty variant's root (`:18` `role="alert"` on the error variant). So the component's two states break the list contract two different ways: populated → children are `article` (D-4), empty → the single child is `status`. Measured live by another seat: registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:16687 `"lists": [{"cls":"palette-card-grid grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]", "childRoles":["status"]}]` on /#/browse. ARIA 1.2 `list` Required Owned Elements = `listitem`; axe `aria-required-children` (serious). This is the axes' central blind spot: all three files are largely ABOUT the empty state (C:9,11; D:11,12,15; L:9,12) and none of them looked at what the empty plate does to the role the same file declares nineteen lines above it. It is also the finding that survives any fix to D-4 — moving `role="listitem"` onto PaletteCard cures the populated state and leaves this one untouched.

missed.claim: The `emptyAction` CTA slot has never had a consumer. A design ruling recorded in the file as surviving was never instantiated, so the empty plate ends in an instruction to go somewhere else with no control that goes there.
missed.proof: `grep -rn "emptyAction|empty-action" demo/ src/` returns exactly two hits, both the declaration itself: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 and :29. The two consumers pass only text — PalettesPane.vue:78-80 and BrowsePane.vue:84-86. The file's own ruling at :19-20 states "The CTA slot survives on the caption" (T.W6.5 · Lane S · R12), and demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:9 advertises "optional hint + CTA slot". Both hint strings are navigations to a place the user must find unaided — "Add colors above, then save the set." (PalettesPane.vue:80) and "Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall." (BrowsePane.vue:86) — while the SIBLING error plate on the same route does carry a real control (BrowsePane.vue:68-77, a `Retry` Button in `#action`). So on one screen the failure state is actionable and the invitation state is a sentence. Corroborated: registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:831 (live accessible text of the /#/palettes plate with `0` elements matching `button, a, [tabindex]`) and :24828. C-2 and L-4 both analysed this slot's typing; neither checked whether anything passes it.

missed.claim: The list has no accessible name, and two unnamed instances can be on screen at once — while the decorative loading containers beside them are the elements that got labelled, on roles where ARIA prohibits naming.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:2-6 declares `role="list"` with no `aria-label` / `aria-labelledby`, and neither consumer supplies one (PalettesPane.vue:75-81, BrowsePane.vue:80-91 pass only `empty*` and `grid-class`); the component exposes no prop for it (:38-44). At desktop the router mounts BrowsePane and PalettesPane side by side — registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:5387 measures both panes at 1440 (`adminRect` 512w + `companionRect` 512w, `companionHeadingText: "My Palettes"`) — so AT can meet two structurally identical unnamed lists in one document with nothing distinguishing the public commons from the user's own library. The inversion makes it worse: BrowsePane.vue:47 and :128 DO carry `aria-label="Loading palettes"` / `"Loading more palettes"`, but on bare `<div>`s whose implicit role is `generic`, which ARIA 1.2 §5.2.8.4 places in the name-prohibited set (corroborated at registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:26448, :72660). The names were spent on the elements that cannot use them and withheld from the one element that can. No axis mentions naming the list at all — D-4 reaches the list role and stops at its children.

missed.claim: The empty↔populated swap is the one unchoreographed state change on the Browse route, and it is the one the user triggers most often.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40 wraps loading / error / wall in `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`, and the comment at :30-39 makes the intent explicit — "ONE surface, NEW content … the developing plates SETTLE into the wall … instead of a hard v-if POP". But empty↔populated happens INSIDE the single `key="wall"` branch, at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:22 `v-if="empty"`, with no Transition and no `key` change — so it pops. The transition the route paid for covers the once-per-visit boot, while every keystroke in the SearchBar (BrowsePane.vue:10-14) that crosses the zero-results boundary gets the hard cut the comment disowns. Not a reduced-motion claim: the global neutraliser at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 is untouched by this, and audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §7.4 lists `PaletteCardGrid` C·D·L as "no motion content", so no quarantined row (M-xx) is being carried here.

missed.claim: The layout constants are the only un-narrated line in a file that narrates everything else, and the arbitrary-value reach is against the house rule.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]` carries no comment in a 53-line file whose other 17 lines of comment cite tranche, wave, lane and ruling. `min-h-[120px]` is an arbitrary-value escape where the scale utility exists (`min-h-30` = 30 × the default `--spacing` 0.25rem = 120px; no `--spacing` override is present in demo/styles or glass-ui's theme), and demo/DESIGN.md:385 records the house rule that arbitrary reaches collapse to first-class utilities post-D.W4 Lane A, with "truly-bespoke residuals (≤ 5) carry an inline rationale" — this one carries none. The 120px floor is also inert in every state that matters (the empty plate's `py-8` plus trio plus three text lines exceeds it) and active only in the one-short-card case, where it opens a void under a single card — and, ironically, is the only condition under which the last card's bottom caster escapes the clip described above. All three axes quote this exact class string in their receipts and none remark on it.

unproven: Whether a Tailwind `contain-*` utility passed through `gridClass` can defeat the scoped `contain: content` rule. I refute it statically on cascade grounds — Vue compiles the scoped selector to `.palette-card-grid[data-v-hash]`, (0,2,0) and unlayered, versus a (0,1,0) utility inside `@layer utilities`, and unlayered wins regardless of specificity — but the shipped stylesheet's layer emission is a build fact. A single `getComputedStyle(grid).contain` read with `grid-class="contain-none"` would settle it. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE (does not change the C-4/D-3/L-2 verdict, which rests on three other refutations).

Whether the unchoreographed empty↔populated swap reads as a perceptible pop at the shipped frame rate, or is masked by the SearchBar's own input latency. The absence of a Transition is proven statically; the perceptual severity is not. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Whether two unnamed `role="list"` regions are simultaneously present in the AT tree at the dual-pane breakpoint. The dual mount is measured by another seat (registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:5387) and the missing name is proven from source, but I did not observe both lists in one accessibility tree. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Whether the o9 TRUE-EMPTY oracles and walk.spec.ts run as a hard CI gate. registry/DEFECT-LEDGER.md:24311 asks for the e2e smoke project to be added to .github/workflows/ci.yml "as a hard step", which implies it is not; I did not verify the workflow. This affects only how much credit the superlative on those oracles deserves, not the C-5 verdict (which turns on the assertion's own logic, not on whether it runs).
superlatives: THE FRAGMENT-ROOT COMMENT — demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11. Five lines that state a constraint, name its mechanism, and name the exact remote consumer that depends on it ("PalettesPane reads `$el` for useSortable — a fragment root resolves $el to the comment node, not the <div>"), and are PLACED so as to be self-demonstrating: the comment is the div's first child, which is precisely the thing it warns about. Verified accurate against demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:180-183. This is the rare comment that survives its author — a maintainer who moves it up one line is told, in advance, what will break and where. Both C-5 and L-5 read this comment and neither credited it while faulting what it protects.

THE DESIGN RULING IS EXECUTABLE, NOT JUST RECORDED — PaletteCardGrid.vue:13-20 records WHY true-empty is the invitation alone (no ghost-card filler; the ShadowPalette species demoted to one standing seat), cross-references EmptyState's own N-3 clause, and demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:29-38 independently states the matching half — the two files agree without either being generated from the other. Then e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187 and :203 pin it as assertions on BOTH hosts ("TRUE EMPTY: the trio + dashes, zero fillers", with an `assertNoFillers` helper). A ratified design ruling that is legible in the source, honoured across a file boundary, and enforced by a named oracle is materially better than the corpus's blanket SOURCE-RED implies, and it directly refutes L-3's "undocumented child behavior".

THE THREE-STATE COMPOSITION LIVES AT THE RIGHT ALTITUDE — demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40-119 renders loading, transport failure and collection as three sibling branches of one `<Transition mode="out-in">`, with the error plate rendered OUTSIDE the list, given `variant="error"`, and carrying a real Retry Button (:61-78) — while the grid stays a dumb presentational leaf. This is exactly the separation D-5 and L-1 demand be built INTO the grid; it already ships one level up, which is where pane policy belongs. The audit asked a leaf to grow a state machine it would have had to be handed anyway.

TWO CHARACTERS OF FORWARD-COMPATIBILITY, NO CLEVERNESS — PaletteCardGrid.vue:23 `class="col-span-full"` on the empty plate. A no-op today at `grid-cols-1`, and exactly right the day `gridClass` changes the column count — which is the one thing `gridClass` is plausibly for. Small, correct, and unremarked by all three axes, two of which spent a finding each attacking `gridClass` as unbounded.

THE ERROR PLATE'S RESTRAINT — demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 and :90 encode a genuinely good distinction ("loading ≠ empty, error ≠ empty"): the error variant DROPS the eyebrow, the ghost trio and the second invitation, keeps a quiet destructive glyph, puts the machine string on a Fira detail line, and carries the only real action on the route. Q6's "error surfaces drop the annotations" is the kind of ruling most design systems state and then violate at the first incident; here the variant is structurally incapable of re-inviting.

confirmed.id: L2-1 / L-1 / C-2 / D-2 / D2-4c (latch + blast radius)
confirmed.claim: One ErrorBoundary wraps the whole two-pane grid; `caught` is component-local state on a component whose lifetime is the app's, so a single pane throw kills both panes and latches every subsequent route dead while the dock keeps accepting navigation.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:123-203, challenge-L-library-r1.md:62-133, challenge-C-implementation.md:249-266, challenge-D-design.md:217-262. LIVE: demo/color-picker/App.vue:50 opens `<ErrorBoundary>` immediately inside `<main class="pane-main">` (:47) and closes at :140, wrapping `.pane-container` (:55-139) and all three PaneSlot sites (:83, :101, :127). demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:55 `const caught = ref(false)`; cleared only in `reset()` (:71-75); no route watcher, no `:key`. ErrorBoundary.vue:35 `<slot v-else />` — while caught, App's entire pane subtree is not rendered, so a route change re-renders nothing. Verified structurally; live latch numbers are the axes' probes.

killed.id: L-1 cure markup (inherited by L2-1 cure step 1)
killed.claim: challenge-L-library-r1.md:117-126 prescribes `<Transition><KeepAlive :max><PaneErrorBoundary :key="liveKey"><component :is="liveComponent" :key="liveKey"/></PaneErrorBoundary></KeepAlive></Transition>`, asserting ':key="liveKey" on the boundary is the whole fix for the latch: caught cannot outlive its subject'. challenge-L-library.md:194-196 inherits it ('Keying the boundary on liveKey makes caught structurally incapable of outliving its subject').
killed.refutation: STRUCTURALLY UNSOUND as written. `KeepAlive` caches its single child vnode by `vnode.key` and DEACTIVATES rather than destroys it. Making `PaneErrorBoundary` the direct child of `<KeepAlive :max>` means the cache holds the BOUNDARY instance keyed by `liveKey`, so `caught === true` is preserved on deactivation and restored verbatim when the user navigates back to that view (until LRU eviction at `:max`) — reproducing the exact latch the cure exists to kill, at pane granularity. demo/shell/PaneSlot.vue:120-127 shows the live shape: KeepAlive's child today IS the pane, and App.vue:88/:107/:133 right-size `:max` to distinct pane counts. The boundary must sit OUTSIDE KeepAlive, or the fallback must be rendered by the seat (challenge-D-design.md:364-371's D2-7 cure, which does not have this flaw). This does not touch the L2-1 defect, only its prescription.

missed.claim: `useDevicePixelSnap` is permanently disarmed — and retains a detached DOM subtree — the first time this boundary fires. Its observers are wired to App's lifetime, not to the element's, and the boundary destroys that element out from under them.
missed.proof: demo/color-picker/App.vue:238-239 binds `useDevicePixelSnap(paneContainer)`, where `paneContainer` is the template ref on `.pane-container` (App.vue:56) — the element that sits INSIDE `<ErrorBoundary>` (:50-140). demo/color-picker/composables/useDevicePixelSnap.ts does all `observe()` wiring in `onMounted` (`ro = new ResizeObserver(schedule); ro.observe(host)` plus one `ro.observe(wrapper)` per `.pane-wrapper`; `mo = new MutationObserver(schedule); mo.observe(host, {childList:true, subtree:true})`; three document/window listeners) and all teardown in `onBeforeUnmount`. Both hooks belong to App, which never unmounts. When `caught` flips, ErrorBoundary.vue:35's `v-else` destroys `.pane-container` and every `.pane-wrapper`: (1) the ResizeObserver and MutationObserver stay bound to the now-detached nodes, holding the old pane subtree alive — a real retention leak; (2) the capture-phase `transitionend`/`animationend` listeners keep firing `onSettle`, which now evaluates `container.value?.contains(...)` against a null ref; (3) after `reset()` a NEW `.pane-container` mounts and nothing re-observes it, because `onMounted` cannot run again — so the S.W5-10 corner-AA cure (the composable's entire stated purpose, useDevicePixelSnap.ts:1-24) is silently dead for the rest of the session. All three axes enumerated the blast radius in terms of panes and KeepAlive caches (C-2, L-1, D-2); none enumerated its composable-level cost, and this is the one that survives even a successful retry.

killed.id: N-1 (D pass 2, the file's headline BLOCKER)
killed.claim: "The four corners of the S×V domain are not hit-testable … pure white and the pure fully-saturated hue cannot be selected by any input this component accepts. A colour picker that cannot pick white." (challenge-D-design.md:19-21,105-140)
killed.refutation: FALSE, and refuted by the corpus's own evidence. (1) SOURCE: MiniColorPicker.vue:129 takes `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown, so every subsequent `pointermove` is delivered to the canvas even outside its box, and :138-139 clamps with `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, …))`. Press anywhere in the interior and drag past the top-left corner ⇒ sat=0, val=1 ⇒ `currentHex` = `#ffffff` exactly. It is also a stable fixed point: `#ffffff` re-decodes at :112-119 to max=1, d=0 ⇒ `val=1, sat=0`, `return` (hue kept). Same for the top-right corner ⇒ the pure hue. (2) IN-CORPUS PROOF: challenge-C's own screenshot, evidence/mini-picker-edges.png (cited at challenge-C-implementation.md:15,185) — I opened it — shows the LIVE component with the readout reading `#ffffff` and the thumb parked in the top-left corner. The state N-1 declares unreachable is photographed in the same component directory. (3) The probes only ever tapped: probe-D2-4.mjs:47-52 and probe-D2-3.mjs:44 use `page.mouse.click(x,y)`; no drag arm was run, so the measurement cannot support a claim quantified over "any input". RESIDUAL, and it is MINOR not BLOCKER: `rounded-lg` (:10) does clip a ~13.7px² quarter-disc per corner out of the TAP hit area — worth fixing, and worth noting that the prescribed cure ("rounding applied as a clip on paint only") is not achievable on the element that owns the hit area; it needs an inner clipped paint layer, or simply the drag path that already works.

killed.claim: "The hue rail's right end does not actuate … the same `rounded-full` hit-clip as N-1" (challenge-D-design.md:319-331)
killed.refutation: PROBE ARTIFACT. probe-D2-3.mjs:68-69 clicks at `rail.x + rail.width * 1.0` — exactly `rail.right`, the first coordinate OUTSIDE a box that spans [x, x+width). Nothing was clicked. The attribution is self-refuting on their own data: the `fx = 0` arm clicked the LEFTMOST pixel at the vertical centre and DID actuate (`left: 0%`), yet a `rounded-full` 12px pill has zero horizontal inset precisely at its vertical centre — so if a radius clip were the mechanism, the left end would have failed identically. Independent counter-evidence: evidence/mini-picker-edges.png shows the handle at `left:100%` (hue 360, half-moon at the right end), i.e. the rail's right extreme is reachable in the live product. The second half of N-7 (the handle is 50% clipped by the rail's own `overflow-hidden` at :26 against `-translate-x-1/2` at :33) stands and is MINOR.

killed.claim: "Both markers are fill-blind by construction … the SV thumb's fill fails [3:1] everywhere (1.03–1.10)" filed as part of a MAJOR (challenge-D-design.md:221-255)
killed.refutation: The fill half is not a defect — it is the canonical design. The repo's own reference instrument fills its marker with the sampled colour too: useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:62 sets `backgroundColor: cssColorOpaque.value` on the WatercolorDot, exactly as MiniColorPicker.vue:19 sets `background: currentHex`. A colour marker whose interior is the colour is the point of a colour marker. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 asks 3:1 of "visual information required to identify components and states" — that is the BOUNDARY (the ring), not the specimen fill; measuring fill-vs-field contrast and calling it a failure would condemn every swatch in the product. What survives, and it is the real finding, is the RING: a scheme-invariant `border-white` (:18, :33) measured at 1.283:1 against the rail track at hue 60. That is the same defect L-4 already owns structurally (the luma-flip helper was dropped), so the row is double-counted across axes.

killed.claim: "12 px hue rail (half the WCAG 2.2 minimum)" / "12 CSS px against a 24px WCAG 2.2 floor" (challenge-C-implementation.md:163-173; challenge-D-design-pass1-c654824e.md:394-408)
killed.refutation: SC 2.5.8 (Target Size Minimum, AA) is MET via its Spacing exception, so the citation fails even though the ergonomic point is fair. The exception asks that a 24px-diameter circle centred on each undersized target not intersect another target. The rail is 12px tall (`h-3`, :26) with `mt-2` = 8px above it and the output row `mt-2` = 8px below (:39). Circle radius 12 from the rail's centre: upward 12 − 6 = 6px beyond the rail's own edge, against an 8px gap to the SV field ⇒ clears by 2px; downward identically ⇒ clears by 2px. No intersection, exception satisfied. What remains is a legitimate design/touch-ergonomics finding (a 12px DRAG surface is hostile on touch), and PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 §5.7 — re-read verbatim — actually supports the file's own position that "visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities", i.e. the cure is an invisible seat, not a fatter rail.

killed.claim: "The internal spacing is five unrelated literals and none of them come from the producer ladder … three are hard-coded consumer literals" (challenge-D-design.md:294-314)
killed.refutation: Two of the three "hard-coded consumer literals" are producer-ladder-derived by construction. In Tailwind v4, `mt-2` (:26, :39) compiles to `margin-top: calc(var(--spacing) * 2)` and `gap-1.5` (:39) to `calc(var(--spacing) * 1.5)` — and the challenge's own census (challenge-D-design.md:304) records `--spacing = 0.25rem` coming from the producer theme. They are not literals and they are not off-ladder; they are the linear ladder. What actually survives is a much narrower INFO: the overlay's φ-derived padding (`--overlay-pad-block = --overlay-pad-inline × 1.272`, popover-BQGYXZyO.js:153) and the linear `--spacing` ladder are two rhythms that do not relate — a producer-side observation, not a consumer violation, and not grounds for the MAJOR grade.

killed.claim: "This component … has no forced-colors arm: no `forced-color-adjust`, no `@media (forced-colors)` block … anywhere" / "N-3 cannot be patched by adding a `@media (forced-colors)` block" / "N-3's generalisation is new and has no owner yet" (challenge-D-design.md:214-215, 468-469, 494)
killed.refutation: The defect is real (I confirm it above) but all three cure/carry claims are false. demo/styles/foundation.css:665-696 is a designed, named, two-tier forced-colors policy (U-F57 / BR-5) whose tier 1 applies `forced-color-adjust: none` to a declared COLOUR-SURFACE ROSTER — `canvas, .spectrum-picker, .gamut-overlay, .atmosphere-canvas, [data-glass-field-canvas], .gradient-rail, .rail-handle, .readout-rail, .swatch-row > *, .generate-swatch, .shadow-swatch, .goo-blob-canvas, .watercolor-swatch, .glass-slider[data-variant="spectrum"] .slider-range, [data-color-surface]` — and the same roster is reused for `@media print` at :829-838. So (a) the mechanism exists and is exactly the `@media (forced-colors)` block declared impossible; (b) `forced-color-adjust: none` is the spec-sanctioned treatment for surfaces whose content IS colour, which the repo already applies to the canonical SV plate `.spectrum-picker`; (c) the generalisation has an owner, and the roster even ships `[data-color-surface]` at :694 as a generic opt-in hook with ZERO current consumers. The true finding is an enrolment omission with a two-attribute cure — see my MISSED row.

missed.claim: The trigger swatch and its accessible name go stale and then silently revert the filter. `pickerHex` is written ONLY by the picker; a typed search never updates it and `Clear all` never resets it — while the swatch's fill AND its accessible name are bound to it.
missed.proof: LIVE: SearchFilterBar.vue:77-78 binds both `:style="{ backgroundColor: pickerHex }"` and `:aria-label="`Open color picker, current color ${pickerHex}`"`. `pickerHex` is assigned at exactly two sites, :176 and :181, both fed from MiniColorPicker's own output. `applyColorSearch` (:213-225) reads `colorText` and emits the search but never writes `pickerHex`; `onClearAll` (:227-232) clears `colorText` and `colorSearchActive` but never `pickerHex`. Consequence chain, all in source: type `#ff0000` → Enter (:95) → the route filters on red, while the swatch still paints AND announces `current color #4488cc`; open the picker and it shows #4488cc (its only inbound channel is MiniColorPicker.vue:110-125); press its Search (:51) → SearchFilterBar.vue:180-187 silently reverts the live filter to #4488cc. After `Clear all filters` the swatch still advertises the cleared colour. All three axes filed the typed-value clobber (D-5, N-2, L-7); none noticed that the component's only PERSISTENT representation of "current colour" — the one an AT user hears — is never synchronised in the other direction. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:83 (verbatim): "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit."

missed.claim: MiniColorPicker's two colour surfaces are the only colour-display surfaces in the demo that were never enrolled in the repo's own forced-colors roster — and the roster already ships the opt-in hook they need, unused.
missed.proof: LIVE: demo/styles/foundation.css:678-695 (`@media (forced-colors: active)`, tier 1) enumerates every colour-display surface in the product by name and grants it `forced-color-adjust: none`; the twin at :829-838 does the same for print. `.sv-canvas` (MiniColorPicker.vue:10,159) and the hue rail (:24-27, which carries no class at all) appear in neither. killed.claim: 'The four corners of the S×V domain are not hit-testable … pure white and the pure fully-saturated hue cannot be selected by any input this component accepts. A colour picker that cannot pick white.' (challenge-D-design.md:17-22, :105-141) — graded BLOCKER and named the strongest defect of the pass.
killed.refutation: REFUTED at the headline. The component clamps pointer coordinates into the domain and holds pointer capture, so the corners are reachable by drag. MiniColorPicker.vue:129 takes `setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` on pointerdown, which per Pointer Events routes ALL subsequent pointermove for that pointer to `.sv-canvas` regardless of hit-testing or element bounds; MiniColorPicker.vue:138-139 then clamps: `sat = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (e.clientX-rect.left)/rect.width))`, `val = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, 1-(e.clientY-rect.top)/rect.height))`. Press anywhere in the interior and drag up-and-left past the corner ⇒ sat=0, val=1 ⇒ in :85-105 with s=0 we get p=q=t=v=1 ⇒ `#ffffff`. Top-right identically gives the pure hue. The probe that produced the verdict never dragged: probe-D2-4.mjs:47-53 issues `page.mouse.click(x, y)` per corner and reads `document.elementFromPoint`, i.e. it measured tap-actuation only. What survives is a tap-only dead quarter-disc of ~13.7 px² per corner from `rounded-lg` (MiniColorPicker.vue:10) — a real but MINOR ergonomic defect, not a silently truncated colour domain, and not a BLOCKER. The prescribed cure ('the paint geometry and the hit geometry must be separate concerns') is aimed at a problem the clamp already solves. The same over-read weakens D2-N-7 (challenge-D-design.md:319-332): the rail's right cap does not actuate on tap, but `updateHue` (:149-154) clamps to [0,360] under capture, and hue 360 ≡ hue 0, so no hue is lost.

killed.claim: '12 px against the 24 px floor of WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum, AA)' (challenge-C-implementation.md:163, :170-173; repeated at challenge-D-design-pass1:394-407 as 'a 24px WCAG 2.2 floor').
killed.refutation: REFUTED on the corpus's own measurements. SC 2.5.8 carries a Spacing exception: an undersized target conforms if a 24 CSS px diameter circle centred on its bounding box does not intersect another target (or another undersized target's circle). The D pass-2 census (challenge-D-design.md:59-63) measures the rail at 174×12 with `rail margin-top 8` above and `row margin-top 8` below — matching MiniColorPicker.vue:26 (`h-3 mt-2`) and :39 (`mt-2`). A 24px circle centred on the rail's bbox spans −6…+18 relative to the rail's 12px box, i.e. it stops 2px short of the SV field above and 2px short of the output row below. No intersection ⇒ the Spacing exception is satisfied ⇒ SC 2.5.8 is not shown to fail. The physical finding (a 12px drag rail is a poor manual target, and it is undersized relative to the repo's own 44px radio floor) stands on ergonomics; the normative AA-failure citation does not, and it is asserted twice across two axes.

killed.claim: 'demo/styles/utils.css:9-11 re-declares .fira-code … The local copy shadows the producer's and drops its ligature settings.' (challenge-D-design-pass1-c654824e.md:496-499)
killed.refutation: REFUTED. demo/styles/utils.css:9-11 is `.fira-code { font-family: var(--font-mono); }` — a single declaration. The producer utility (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/typography/utilities.css) is `@utility fira-code { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-feature-settings: "liga", "calt"; }`. Both rules match the same element (MiniColorPicker.vue:44 `class="fira-code text-caption …"`), and `font-feature-settings` is declared by EXACTLY ONE of them, so nothing overrides it — the ligature settings apply whichever rule wins the `font-family` tie, and both rules set that property to the identical value anyway. The duplication is real and worth deleting; the stated consequence ('drops its ligature settings') does not follow and is the only thing that made the row a defect rather than a tidy-up.

killed.claim: 'setPointerCapture is taken at :129 / :144 and never released' — offered as part of the BLOCKER's mechanism (challenge-C-implementation.md:30-36).
killed.refutation: REFUTED as stated, and it misdirects the cure. Pointer capture release is a UA obligation, not the author's: the spec releases implicit/explicit capture on `pointerup` and `pointercancel`, and when the capturing element is removed from the document the UA fires `lostpointercapture` and releases. So capture is in fact released on every one of the interruption paths C-1 enumerates (Escape, outside click, the `search` emit at SearchFilterBar.vue:183, route change, iOS scroll takeover). The defect that actually survives — and the one the reproduction demonstrates — is narrower and entirely about the non-reactive booleans: MiniColorPicker.vue:79-80 are cleared ONLY by :133/:148 on `@pointerup`, and the component binds no `@pointercancel`, no `@lostpointercapture` and no `onUnmounted`. A reader who fixed 'the unreleased capture' (by adding `releasePointerCapture`) would ship a still-broken component; the fix is to clear the flags on cancel/lost-capture/unmount, which is exactly what SpectrumCanvas.vue:168-175 does at :172-174 and NOT what its `releaseCapture()` at :81-91 does.

killed.claim: 'Two quantisation laws, one concept' — that `roundHalfEven` vs `Math.round` is the sole cause, and that the re-run 'rules out a deeper algebraic error' (challenge-L-library.md:124-127, :513-516).
killed.refutation: PARTIALLY REFUTED — the magnitude claim survives, the sole-cause attribution does not. Re-running against dist/subpaths/color.js: at the EXACT value 0.5 the two agree (`comp(0,0,0.5) === lib(0,0,0.5) === "#808080"`), because roundHalfEven(127.5) → floor 127 is odd → 128, identical to half-up. The banker's-rounding story only bites where the .5 lands on an EVEN floor (v=0.3 → 76.5 → library 76 / component 77, as cited). But a SECOND, uncited mechanism is present: src/color/operations.ts:307 treats a value as a half whenever `|fraction − 0.5| < Number.EPSILON · max(1,|value|)`, i.e. it snaps NEAR-halves too. At v = 0.49999999999999994 — precisely what the axis's own accumulating loop (`for (let V = 0; V <= 1.0001; V += 0.05)`, probe-L9-hsv-drift.mjs:56) produces — the library returns `#808080` (128) and `Math.round` returns `#7f7f7f` (127): the divergence runs the OPPOSITE direction from the stated mechanism, and it is the very first row of the persisted probe's own mismatch table. Consequence: the drift probe's 12.419% is partly an artifact of float accumulation in the grid, and 'rules out a deeper algebraic error' is unproven. What I do confirm by independent exact-fraction sweep (si/20, vi/20): 11.2891% of 53361 samples diverge with max |Δ| = 1 LSB. The defect is real; its published explanation is incomplete.

missed.claim: The parent's entire pending/loading arm is unreachable dead code: `searching` can never be true at render time, so the spinner, the disabled attribute and the disabled styling are all structurally dead — which inverts what D2-N-11 and D-17 concluded.

Vue flushes the component update only after the event handler returns, by which time `searching` is false again. Therefore `:98 :disabled="searching"`, the `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:pointer-events-none` classes at :99, and `<Loader2 v-if="searching" class="animate-spin">` at :102 are all unreachable states, and the `async` keyword is decorative. missed.claim: Error posture: the only failure path in the whole colour-search feature is an uncaught `throw`, held closed solely by the masking regex that L-7 correctly indicts.

Its two callers handle nothing: `applyColorSearchFromPicker` (:180-187) calls it bare inside a click handler, and `applyColorSearch` (:213-225) wraps it in `try { … } finally { … }` with NO `catch` — the `finally` only resets `searching`, so any throw propagates out of the DOM event handler. There is no `aria-invalid`, no message, no live region (D-17 pass1:474 noted the child's silent `return` but not the parent's throw). This is latent only because :218's `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i` gate narrows the input to something that cannot fail — i.e. the masking fallback is the sole thing keeping the throw path closed, and the placeholder at :92 already promises the input that opens it. missed.claim: Pointer capture is taken on `e.target` rather than `e.currentTarget`, diverging from the canonical instrument and unguarded against the throwing case.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:129 `(e.target as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` and :144 the same for the rail. The canonical instrument uses the currentTarget explicitly: SpectrumCanvas.vue:135 `const el = event.currentTarget as HTMLElement;` then :148 `el.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId)`. The subject works today only because both thumbs are `pointer-events-none` (:18, :33), so target and currentTarget happen to coincide; any child gaining pointer events moves capture onto an element whose rect is NOT the one `updateCanvas`/`updateHue` measure (:135-139, :150-153), silently skewing the mapping. `setPointerCapture` also throws `NotFoundError` for a pointerId that is no longer active, and neither call site guards it — the canonical instrument's only defensive `try/catch` is on the release side (SpectrumCanvas.vue:83-87). C-1 cites the capture lines but reads them as a leak (see kill) rather than as a contract divergence.

missed.claim: `hex` is shadowed three lines apart and means two different things; the two identifiers are the two ends of the L-9 feedback loop.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:65 destructures the prop `const { open, hex } = defineProps<…>()`. MiniColorPicker.vue:107 then writes `watch(currentHex, (hex) => emit("update:hex", hex))`, whose parameter shadows that prop with the OUTBOUND value. MiniColorPicker.vue:110 immediately writes `watch(() => hex, (incomingHex) => …)`, where `hex` is the prop again — the INBOUND value. The file's most consequential defect is a loop between those two watchers, and its two ends are spelled with the same four letters in adjacent statements. No axis flagged it; D-21 (pass1:520-523) reviewed exactly this region for emit-idiom hygiene and did not see the shadow.

missed.claim: The HSV→RGB switch has no `default` arm and pre-seeds black, so 'I cannot compute this colour' and 'this colour is black' are the same output — a masking posture inside the one function whose job is colour truth.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:94 `let r = 0, g = 0, b = 0;` followed by `switch (i % 6)` at :95 with cases 0-5 only and no `default`. Any `i` outside that set — NaN from a malformed prop (the C-5 `#zzzzzz` path), or any future negative hue — falls through to the seeded zeros and emits `#000000` as a successful result. The published surface takes the opposite posture at exactly this boundary: src/color/operations.ts:313-330 `toRgba8` returns a `Result` and errs with `color_invalid_input` / `color_missing_alpha` rather than substituting a value, and demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:213-217 `pickerColorToHex` uses `valueOrThrow` so the failure cannot be mistaken for a colour. C-5 measured the `#zzzzzz` instance (challenge-C-implementation.md:209) but framed it as a parse bug; the structural point is that black is the file's designed answer to 'unknown'.

superlatives: `demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts` — 35 lines whose entire purpose is to make a copied constant impossible, and which say so in their own docstring (:8-9 'Share the function, never copy the constant (`overlay-amendment.md §4.1`)'), export the threshold as a named symbol (:20 `SPECTRUM_LUMA_FLIP = 0.5`), and hand callers a predicate rather than a number (:33-35). Three instruments read the field through it (WatercolorDot border, gamut overlay ink, slider needle) and therefore cannot disagree. Provenance of its quality: the model is analytically exact for the plate it describes — my closed-form integral of its own predicate over the unit square, 2[u − ½ln u]₀.₅¹ = 0.30685, lands on L-4's independently measured 30.70%.

`vite.config.ts:37-50` — the seven demo self-aliases are GENERATED from `package.json#exports` with anchored `^…$` regexes, so the demo is structurally incapable of importing a specifier a real npm consumer could not write, and the reason for the anchoring (an object-form prefix rewrite that turned `@mkbabb/value.js/math` into a path INTO the dist FILE and broke the R-era demo boot) is recorded in place at :30-36. `SpectrumCanvas.vue` is a COMPLETE pointer contract, which is rare: capture tracked in a locals pair with a `try/catch` release for the detached-element case (:78-91), `pointercancel` AND `lostpointercapture` both bound (:18-19) with the lost-capture path clearing drag state (:168-175), an rAF coalescer that FLUSHES its pending sample on stop rather than dropping it (:187-200), and an `onUnmounted` that releases capture, cancels the frame and nulls the pending coords (:217-224). Four separate cures, each of which the subject omits — and the raw-coords design at :58-63 ('Raw spectrum coords to avoid HSV roundtrip jitter. Persists after mouseup so the dot stays where the user placed it.') is a comment that diagnoses L-9 four years of altitude above it.

The third is `demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:29`: `if (parent.closest("pre, code, mark, script, .katex")) return NodeFilter.FILTER_REJECT;` — inside a `document.createTreeWalker(body, NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT, …)` (:24-40) that then REPLACES every accepted text node with a fragment containing `<mark class="cs-name">` elements (:45-65). The guard is keyed on KaTeX's OWN class `.katex`, not on anything `Katex.vue` owns. Today it holds — for both modes the injected tree is `div.inline-block > span.katex…` or `div.inline-block > span.katex-display > span.katex`, so every katex text node has a `.katex` ancestor, including the raw-LaTeX `<annotation>` inside `.katex-mathml`. But it makes the prescribed cures unsafe in a way none of them accounts for: challenge-L's gestalt cure (:450-469) emits `<figure class="math-display">` / `<span class="math-inline">` from a build-time transform, and challenge-D's D-4 cure (:228-231) proposes dropping to `output: "html"` and designating the `<annotation>` as the selectable payload. Either one moves math text out from under a `.katex` ancestor, at which point the TreeWalker starts splicing `<mark>` elements INTO KaTeX's span lattice — every occurrence of the active colour-space name inside a formula — with no test (L-6 confirmed: zero) to catch it. The cure list must carry this guard as a fourth edit.

"MathML-only delegated glyph metrics to each browser's math engine — WebKit's MathML-Core is the least mature, an S-22 (Safari-truth) risk." No demo override exists: grep for `--radius` over the whole demo/ tree returns only DESIGN.md prose, a foundation.css:110 comment and `var(--radius-panel)` at foundation.css:353; demo/styles contains no `--radius` declaration and there is no demo style.css. L's supporting inference (grep for radius-input in demo/styles/ returns nothing, therefore it inherits 0.25rem) is a non-sequitur -- absence in the demo proves nothing about the producer's value. The doc-drift PREMISE survives (DESIGN.md:195 asserts 8px against a token that resolves to 0.625rem), but the number L reports, the reasoning chain, and the 'DEFECT-LEDGER already propagated the stale 8px' downstream claim all rest on a value that cannot be derived from the current bytes. Same figure re-used in challenge-D §2.1 (`textareaRadius: "4px"`) -- equally unreproducible.

killed.id: L-2 mechanism limb #1 / L-1 causal claim
killed.claim: "demo/ui/button/index.ts re-exports the VALUE binding without restating the CONTRACT, so a call site can keep passing a prop the real component deleted and nothing on the path objects" -- and therefore deleting demo/ui/ "makes L-2 a COMPILE ERROR instead of a silent visual regression" / "every one of the 51 sites becomes a compile error".
killed.refutation: REFUTED. `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` is a plain value re-export that preserves the component's full declared type -- vue-tsc resolves props from `ButtonProps` through it exactly as it would through a direct import. There is no type-erasing hop. The actual reason `variant` typechecks green is that the repo sets NO `vueCompilerOptions` in any tsconfig (verified: grep for vueCompilerOptions over tsconfig*.json -> no match), so `strictTemplates` defaults to false and vue-tsc permits unknown attributes as fallthrough. L's own DEFECT-LEDGER cure line concedes this ("one migration of all 51 sites PLUS `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates: true` so the class cannot recur"). Consequence: deleting demo/ui/ would not convert a single one of the 51 sites into a compile error, and the keystone reasoning of L's greenfield lattice ("This is the keystone: it converts L-2's silent visual regression into a type error") is wrong. L-1's factual base (19 barrels, 0 implementations, dual import path) stands and is confirmed separately; only its claimed mechanism and payoff are refuted.

missed.claim: The textarea's focus ring reaches a token that does not exist: `ring-ring/40` resolves through `--color-ring`, which is defined nowhere in glass-ui 7.0.0 or the demo. The intended 40%-alpha ring never paints; only the width survives, falling back to Tailwind's `currentcolor`. This is verbatim the U-F25 defect the repo already diagnosed and cured -- and the cure is a producer utility worn by the very same rendered dialog.
missed.proof: LIVE: demo/palettes/browser/dialog/FlagReportDialog.vue:32 `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40`. Tailwind v4.3.0 (package.json) resolves `ring-<name>` via `--color-<name>`. Exhaustive search: grep for `--color-ring` over node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/ and demo/ returns exactly ONE hit and it is prose -- demo/styles/focus-ring.css:11; grep for `--ring[:;) ]` over glass-ui/dist/styles/ and demo/styles/ returns nothing. glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/bridges.css bridges 60+ `--color-*` keys (--color-input, --color-background, --color-destructive, --color-border ...) and `ring` is not among them; the producer's own focus token is `--focus-ring-color` / `--focus-ring-shadow`, a different name. The repo has already written this defect down: demo/styles/focus-ring.css:9-13 -- "the `--ring`/`--color-ring` token it reached resolved EMPTY -- so even an un-clobbered ring painted nothing" (U.W-A11Y / U-F25) -- and the producer ships the cure as a first-class utility: `.focus-ring:focus-visible { outline:none; border-radius: var(--radius-pill); box-shadow: var(--focus-ring-shadow) }` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/base.css:1), which is the class the producer's own DialogClose wears eight lines away in the same dialog (dialog-TNRDkcE4.js:349). All three axes quoted the class string verbatim (challenge-D-design.md:297-310, challenge-C-implementation.md:357-359, challenge-L-library.md:293-294); none asked whether the token resolves. Repo-wide class (7 other sites). The exact rendered fallback colour is Tailwind-version behaviour and wants a live confirm; the token's non-existence is decisive on the bytes.

missed.claim: The producer had already SOLVED the touch-target overlap, and the consumer's one class un-solved it -- and D-5's prescribed cure would make the overlap worse, not better.
missed.proof: LIVE: glass-ui.css `.radio-group{ --radio-face:1.125rem; --radio-seat:var(--touch-target,2.75rem); --radio-seat-offset:calc((var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face))/-2); gap:calc(var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face)); flex-direction:column; display:flex }`. The producer pairs a -13px seat offset with an exactly compensating 26px gap so 44px hit boxes tile edge-to-edge at a 44px pitch: zero overlap, by construction. FlagReportDialog.vue:16 `class="flex flex-col gap-2"` is three-quarters REDUNDANT (`display:flex` and `flex-direction:column` are already on `.radio-group`) and its one non-redundant token is precisely the one that destroys the compensation; :17-21 then wraps each item in `<div class="flex items-center gap-2">`, so the row height is set by the label line box (22.95px) rather than the seat. challenge-D-design.md:344-346 blames only "an 8px gap on an 18px glyph" and never identifies the producer's compensation rule; its cure at :354-356 -- "`gap` becomes 0 and the rhythm comes from the seat" -- would drop the pitch to 22.95px and GROW the overlap from 13.05px to 21.05px. The correct cure is to delete both the class and the wrapper `<div>` and let `.radio-group` own the rhythm. Neither challenge-C nor challenge-L measured this axis at all.

missed.claim: The dialog never discloses that a report is one-shot and irrevocable -- the single most consequential fact about the action it is asking consent for.
missed.proof: LIVE: api/src/modules/palette/service/flags.ts:38-52 -- the flag insert is unique-key guarded (`code === 11000` -> `ConflictError("Already flagged")`), and no unflag, withdraw or amend route exists in the module. The dialog's ENTIRE copy is `Report Palette` (:9), `Why are you reporting "X"?` (:11), `Additional details (optional)...` (:31), `Cancel` (:39), `Report` (:47). Nothing states that the report cannot be undone, corrected or repeated; nothing states who sees it or what happens next. challenge-C-implementation.md:109-116 USES the irreversibility to grade C-1's severity and :213 enumerates the 409 as a status code, and challenge-L-library.md never touches it -- but no axis files the absent disclosure as a defect of the surface whose entire job is to obtain informed consent for an irreversible moderation act. FlagReportDialog.vue:22-25 -- every radio carries a real <label :for> bound to a real :id. This is the one part of the form that is correctly named: each option has a genuine accessible name AND a text hit target, verified by challenge-C's negative result #3 (label[for="reason-copyright"] click -> {"id":"reason-copyright","checked":"true"}) and by the producer's own aria-label pass-through. Everything the axes say about the group's missing name is true; the ITEMS are exemplary.

FlagReportDialog.vue:5-8 -- the T.W4-6 (T-15/F7) provenance comment names the tranche, the finding id, the producer default it overrides, the register it is joining, and the fact that a producer-root candidate was already recorded with the W4-6 sweep. challenge-D-design.md:459 reads it as "a confession", and it is -- but it is also the reason D-10 could be adjudicated at all. A per-instance override that documents itself as provisional and names its own permanent home is a discipline most overrides in this repo lack.

The component keeps one job in 101 lines with zero lifecycle hooks, listeners, observers, timers and requestAnimationFrame -- challenge-C-implementation.md:594-595 verified this as a negative proof, making the file structurally immune to the constellation-wide PRM-RAF class and to the ValueUnit nesting hazard. Edict 1 (no god modules) is satisfied by a wide margin; challenge-D-design.md:708 and challenge-L's negative-proof block both grant it independently.

challenge-C-implementation.md:562-575, Negative results #1 -- the corpus's single best act of discipline. The seat had a publishable finding (a 1s stalled dialog enter transition, measured opacity: 0, blur(6px), three CSSTransitions at currentTime:0), re-ran the identical trace under WebKit, got currentTime:115 and full settle by 400ms, FALSIFIED ITS OWN FINDING, declined to report it, and published the methodological warning for the fleet instead: any Chromium+SwiftShader screenshot of a glass-reveal overlay in this repo can capture a transparent or blurred element. That warning is worth more to the next twenty seats than the finding would have been.

challenge-D-design.md's in-file measurements reproduce EXACTLY from the tree with no browser at all: the 30.95px radio pitch and 13.05px overlap fall out of --radio-seat/--radio-face/--radio-seat-offset and the label line box; the 16.4px label falls out of --type-small: clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem) at 1440; the 6/24/12/24 gap ladder falls out of the producer's dialog-content-region gap:1rem plus gap-y-1.5, py-2 and gap-3; rgb(11,10,9) falls out of --neutral-0: light-dark(hsl(40 30% 98%), hsl(24 9% 4%)). Measurement that a hostile re-reader can re-derive from source, to two decimal places, without repeating the probe, is the strongest form of provenance in this corpus -- and it stands in sharp contrast to the same seat's cross-file line citations, three of which do not resolve.
